Roll out 0.2.x runners and run fleet before/after interrupt recount (S5).

Source research: task 2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4 ("noticing a high level of interruptions"). Read docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/RESPONSE.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md and the cited GUIDE before coding. Section: RESPONSE.md S5, docs/tasks/2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4/GUIDE-05-commit-push-crash-loop.md (E5 sweep), WIDE_NET Cause 5 + rollout. Survey: q9 (gradual rollout, never force-restart mid-task). Ops + verification, no new unit tests.

Evidence: "Deployed runners are 0.1.0 (main f430f53, 11-11); repo is 0.2.0 with interrupt reasons and deterministic-git-failure handling (046a6391, merged 11-21 09:38 in 7ac148ce). Rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle-converge (docs/runner-update-runbook.md), so lag is expected - but until it lands, every new interrupt is still bare and every commit-hook rejection still crash-loops."

Steps: (1) confirm local-alpha + server2-alpha converge to build containing 046a6391 per docs/runner-update-runbook.md; record GET /runners versions before/after. (2) re-run WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md section 2 counts + GUIDE-07 section 5 fleet script: bare interrupts -> ~0, reasons name Causes 1/3/4, deterministic commit failures surface as FAILED with gitFailure payloads, never interrupts. (3) E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 section 4): for each remaining post-finished interrupt, check kb-<taskId> worktrees (158394ab, db49d6c6, 1cae113f, 7f6220c3) for stage-output-commit presence (present -> Cause 2/4 territory; absent -> Cause 5). Only if E5 finds commit-loop cases 046a6391 does not cover, create a NEW Cause-5 code ticket. (4) record post-rollout counts in task folder as new baseline for S1-S4.

RISK: observe only - do NOT force-restart runners mid-assignment (PROD-ACTION, would create the interrupts being measured). Runs parallel to all code work; only prod CONFIRMATION of S3/S4/S2-runner-half waits on it.

reports.content:
# IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN — S5: Roll out 0.2.x runners and run fleet before/after interrupt recount

Task: `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` (RESPONSE.md S5 of `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4`).
Type: ops + verification. No code changes, no new unit tests.
Date: 2026-11-23. Status: plan (nothing executed yet).

## Goal

Confirm both production runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge via the
normal idle-update channel to a build containing the deterministic-git-failure fix
(`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`), then prove with fleet-wide
before/after counts that the 0.2.x rollout resolves the "bare interrupt" class:
bare interrupts drop to ~0, reasons name Causes 1/3/4, and deterministic commit
failures surface as FAILED completions with `gitFailure` payloads instead of
interrupts. Record the post-rollout counts as the new baseline for S1–S4.

## Success criteria

1. `GET /runners` versions recorded before AND after; both named runners observed
   on a `0.2.x` build whose release contains `046a6391` (verified via
   `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0`, not by version string alone).
2. WIDE_NET §2 counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script re-run on the same scope,
   recorded in the task folder as before/after tables.
3. S5-attributable signals move as predicted: bare interrupts → ~0 on new
   interrupts, `with_reason` names Causes 1/3/4, deterministic commit failures
   appear as FAILED + `gitFailure` (never interrupts). (Cap-escalation and label
   fixes are S1/S6 territory — see §"Attribution boundaries".)
4. E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4) executed for every remaining post-`finished`
   interrupt: each classified commit-present (Cause 2/4) or commit-absent
   (Cause 5 suspect), with evidence or an explicit evidence-gap note.
5. Post-rollout baseline recorded in the task folder and usable by S1–S4 as their
   "before" reference (counts + runner versions + backend build + window dates).
6. Zero forced restarts, zero reaped exhibit worktrees, zero agent re-runs:
   observe-only throughout (q9 constraint).

## Grounded facts (verified 2026-11-23 in this checkout)

- HEAD is `7ac148ce` and contains `046a6391` (verified: `git merge-base
  --is-ancestor 046a6391 HEAD` → YES). `046a6391` is the 17-file
  deterministic-git-failure change (daemon branch, `shared/gitFailure/*`).
- `runner/version.json` reads `runnerVersion: 0.2.0`.
  Release tags `runner-v0.1.0` AND `runner-v0.2.0` both exist, so the 0.2.x
  release is already cut (runbook step 4 done). Remaining rollout gates: the
  backend recommended knob + per-runner idle converge.
- Recommended-knob wiring: `api/config/schema.js` key `runnerRecommendedVersion`
  (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION`), **default `0.1.0`**. The live value
  must be read at execution time — the default alone cannot confirm the rollout
  is switched on (this is survey q1).
- Runner endpoints exist: `GET /runners` → `runnerRegistry.list()` (fleet
  matrix: versions, badges, update status), `GET /runners/monitor`,
  per-runner `pendingCommands`/`requestUpdate` acks (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js`).
- Baseline to beat (WIDE_NET §2, project `0fd41821`, 61 tasks, 2026-11-21):
  118 runner-path interrupts (96 local-alpha / 22 server2-alpha), 49 with
  reason (all cap refusals), 69 bare, 99 ≤15 s after `started` (median 4.7 s),
  15 ≥2 min after `started`, 42 death-streak escalations, 0 server-restart
  interrupts, 100 `Auto-resumed after server restart` rows.
- API base for prod reads: `http://192.168.1.206:3100` (`localhost:3100`
  refuses connections from this runner host, per TICKETS doc).
- E5 exhibits are **already absent on this host**: no `kb-158394ab`,
  `kb-db49d6c6`, `kb-1cae113f`, `kb-7f6220c3` under the server2-alpha work
  root (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_WORK_ROOT=/home/server2/.kainbain/runner-work`,
  only 5 unrelated `kb-*` dirs present). The local-alpha host
  (`192.168.1.206`, `~server`) is unchecked — the sweep must check there
  first and treat absence as an evidence gap with fallbacks (§Phase 2).
- GUIDE-05 §4's path `~/.kainbain/kb-$t` is stale for server2-alpha; the real
  layout is `$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_WORK_ROOT/kb-<taskId>*`. Resolve the work root
  per host before sweeping.

## Survey integration (SURVEY.md + RESPONSE_SURVEY.md)

The task survey (`SURVEY.md`, Round 1, stage-1792362077711) is **generated but
unanswered** (`"answers": {}`); the source survey (`RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q1–q9)
is likewise unanswered. The plan therefore adopts the recommended option of
each question as a reviewable assumption, keeps the question open, and carries
a fallback branch per question:

| Q | Recommended assumption (plan default) | Fallback if answered otherwise |
|---|---|---|
| q1 (knob already on?) | Observe + record; verify knob state read-only, do NOT change it | If "check and switch on": add one backend config change (`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION=0.2.0`), no restarts, recorded with before/after value |
| q2 (read-only prod access?) | Full read-only: backend API + runner journals + worktrees on both hosts | API-only: Phases 1/3/4 proceed, Phase 2 E5 becomes journals-unavailable gap note; "docs only": task cannot execute — re-plan as procedure-only doc |
| q3 (wait for converge?) | Wait-and-watch in the same run until both runners converge, then after-recount | Before-now/stop: deliver BEFORE + E5 + versions now, AFTER as a scheduled follow-up run; never "record mid-rollout as after" |
| q4 (recount scope?) | Same project `0fd41821` only, directly comparable to the 11-21 baseline | All-projects: run the same script per project and keep `0fd41821` as the headline comparison table |
| RESPONSE q9 (rollout pace) | **Hard constraint**: gradual idle-converge, never force-restart mid-task | No fallback — any "faster" answer must come from the human explicitly; the plan refuses to include forced restarts on its own authority |

Execution must re-read both survey files for answers before running anything;
an answered survey overrides the assumption row above.

## Approach — make observation easy, then observe

This task changes nothing; its failure mode is fuzzy, non-reproducible numbers.
So Phase 0 ("make change easy") builds all reusable observation tooling first —
frozen scripts, record templates, access checks, and the BEFORE snapshot — and
only then do the time-ordered phases run. Big/volatile evidence comes early:
the BEFORE recount and the E5 sweep run before the convergence wait, because
interrupts keep accruing and worktree exhibits keep getting reaped (all four
E5 seed exhibits are already absent from this host). The long pole — idle
convergence at most daily per runner — waits in Phase 3 without blocking
Phase 1/2 evidence.

Attribution boundaries (what S5 may and may not claim): S1 (cap counting),
S2-backend (413 limit), S4 (transient tolerance), S6 (labels/counts) all change
the same signals. S5's after-recount MUST record the backend build number
(`GET /deploy/status`) and which sibling fixes have landed, and split new
interrupts by timestamp against each runner's converge time. Only interrupts
timestamped after a runner converged to 0.2.x count as "after" for S5.
`escalated` dropping is an S1 signal, not an S5 gate; the S5 gates are bare→~0,
reasons present, and FAILED+`gitFailure` instead of commit-loop interrupts.

## Phase 0 — Setup: tooling, access, knob state, BEFORE snapshot (first)

0.1 Re-read `SURVEY.md` and `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` for answers; record the
    effective decision per question at the top of the run log.
0.2 Access checks (read-only, stop on first refusal and record it):
    `GET /status/observability`, `GET /tasks?projectId=0fd41821` (expect ~61+
    tasks — confirms project id scope for q4), `GET /runners`,
    `GET /deploy/status` (backend build number), journal read on both hosts,
    work-root listing on both hosts.
0.3 Knob state (q1): record live `runnerRecommendedVersion` /
    `runnerMinVersion` (backend config endpoint or operator-read env).
    Under the default assumption do NOT change them; under the q1-fallback,
    raise recommended to `0.2.0` (config only, no restart) and record old→new.
0.4 Freeze the observation kit in this task folder so S1–S4 re-run identically:
    - `bin/fleet-recount.sh` — GUIDE-07 §5 script pinned to the API base +
      project id, plus a `jq -s` aggregation pass emitting the WIDE_NET §2
      table rows (runner_interrupts, with_reason, bare, ≤15 s, ≥2 min,
      auto_resumed, server_restart, escalated, per-runner split).
    - `bin/runners-snapshot.sh` — `GET /runners` raw JSON → timestamped file.
    - `bin/e5-sweep.sh` — corrected E5 loop resolving `$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_WORK_ROOT`
      per host + journal greps (E3 `Backend 413`, E4 502/`fetch failed`,
      hook/commit lines).
    - `RUN-LOG.md` — timestamped run diary (knob values, backend builds,
      converge times, sibling-fix landings).
0.5 BEFORE snapshot (same run as 0.2): save raw `GET /runners` JSON and run the
    fleet script → `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md` (per-task rows + §2 table). This is the
    "before" half of the rollout proof; everything after compares to it.
0.6 Verify release content: `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0`
    (must print YES — proves the 0.2.0 release actually carries the fix).

Gate: kit committed in folder, BEFORE counts + BEFORE versions saved, knob
state recorded. All later phases are mechanical re-runs of Phase 0 tooling.

## Phase 1 — BEFORE recount analysis (same data as 0.5, second lens)

1.1 Recompute the WIDE_NET §2 table from the BEFORE snapshot and diff it against
    the 11-21 baseline (new interrupts since 11-21 are expected — runners are
    still 0.1.0; every new one should still be bare, which itself re-confirms
    the "until it lands" premise).
1.2 List every post-`finished` interrupt (≥2 min after `started`, or explicit
    `finished`→interrupt pair) with task id + timestamps — this is the E5
    worklist for Phase 2.
1.3 Confirm the reason vocabulary on new interrupts: cap refusals still reasoned,
    everything else bare. Any *reasoned non-cap* interrupt before convergence
    would contradict the "0.1.0 emits no reasons" premise — flag, don't ignore.

Gate: `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md` holds §2 table + diff vs 11-21 + E5 worklist.

## Phase 2 — E5 forensics sweep (early: exhibits are volatile)

For each post-`finished` interrupt from 1.2 (seeds: `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`,
`1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`, plus any new ones from 1.1):

2.1 Worktree check per host (read-only, never reap): resolve the runner work
    root on that host first, then
    `git -C $WORK_ROOT/kb-<taskId>* log --oneline -3` and look for a
    stage-output commit matching the execution window. Present → Cause 2/4
    territory; absent → Cause 5 suspect. Record exact SHAs or exact absence.
2.2 Journal join (same host, same window): `Runner failed:` line text +
    restart-counter deltas — names hook/commit vs 413 vs 502/fetch-fail.
2.3 Fallback chain when a worktree is absent (already the case on server2-alpha
    for all four seeds): (a) check the sibling host; (b) check `origin` for the
    stage-output SHA (pushed = commit succeeded, Cause 2/4); (c) journal line
    alone; (d) if all absent, record an explicit evidence gap — never guess.
2.4 Verdict per interrupt: Cause-2/4 vs Cause-5-covered-by-`046a6391` vs
    Cause-5-NOT-covered. The third verdict is the ONLY trigger for new code:
    if and only if E5 finds commit-loop cases `046a6391` does not cover
    (a deterministic failure class outside `HOOK_REJECTED`/`COMMIT_FAILED`/
    `MERGE_CONFLICT` that still crash-loops on 0.2.x), file a NEW Cause-5
    code ticket with the journal line + worktree state + failing class.

Gate: `E5-SWEEP.md` with one row per post-`finished` interrupt (evidence or
gap) + the ticket/no-ticket decision with reasoning.

## Phase 3 — Convergence watch (the long pole; observe only)

3.1 Poll `GET /runners` on a slow cadence (30–60 min) and snapshot each poll.
    Per runner record: running version + build facts, `updateAvailable` /
    `belowMinimum` / `updateStatus` badges, pending vs acked `requestUpdate`
    (nudge cooldown is 24 h), busy/idle, pinned-vs-Latest.
3.2 Declare a runner converged at the first poll showing a 0.2.x build whose
    release contains `046a6391`; record the converge timestamp per runner in
    `RUN-LOG.md`. Both converged → proceed to Phase 4 (q3 default).
3.3 If a runner stalls (badge never clears past 24–48 h): triage READ-ONLY per
    the runbook ("a runner says out of date") — `entrypoint: direct` vs
    wrapper, `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` opt-out, pinned version, pin
    older than running, recommended knob above every release, `updateStatus`
    failure reason — and record the blocking cause. Fixes (migrate, flip the
    switch, Update button) are PROD-ACTION: propose, do not perform.
3.4 NEVER to speed convergence: force-restart mid-assignment, Update-on-busy,
    reaping worktrees, re-running parked tasks. Any of these manufactures the
    interrupts being measured (q9 / PROD-ACTION ban).

Gate: per-runner converge timestamps, or a stalled-runner triage note with a
named blocking cause. Under the q3-fallback (before-now/stop), Phase 3 becomes
a scheduled follow-up run instead of a same-run wait.

## Phase 4 — AFTER recount + journal sweeps (after both converge)

4.1 AFTER snapshot: raw `GET /runners` JSON + fleet script → `RECOUNT-AFTER.md`
    (§2 table + per-task rows), timestamped ≥ both converge times.
4.2 Split new interrupts at each runner's converge time; evaluate the S5 gates
    on post-converge interrupts only: bare → ~0; reasons name Causes 1/3/4
    (cap strings, setup-fault messages, transient 502/fetch-fail strings);
    deterministic commit failures arrive as FAILED completions carrying
    `gitFailure` payloads (`kind`/`phase`/`summary`) with NO interrupt row.
4.3 Journal sweeps (both hosts, post-converge window): E3 `Backend 413` lines
    (expect none-new after S2 lands; any 413 on 0.2.x must pair with a FAILED
    completion, never a crash loop), E4 502/`fetch failed` crash lines
    (expect crash-restarts to persist until S4 lands — reasons now name them),
    hook/commit lines (expect single `commit failed (...)` + FAILED, no
    restart storm).
4.4 Record confounds: backend build number at AFTER time, which of S1/S2/S4/S6
    have deployed, and any deploys that restarted the backend in-window
    (Cause-6 upkeep: any `interrupted by server restart` row re-opens it).

Gate: `RECOUNT-AFTER.md` with the post-converge-gated verdict per S5 gate
(pass/fail + counts), plus the confound ledger.

## Phase 5 — Baseline record + handoff (closes the task)

5.1 Write `BASELINE.md`: the new S1–S4 reference — BEFORE/AFTER §2 tables,
    per-runner versions + converge timestamps, backend builds, window dates,
    E5 verdicts, open evidence gaps, and the exact re-run commands (Phase 0 kit).
5.2 Handoff notes: unblock prod CONFIRMATION of S3/S4/S2-runner-half (code work
    never waited); S1/S6 confirm against `BASELINE.md` + their own deploys.
    If 2.4 triggered, link the new Cause-5 ticket; otherwise state explicitly
    that no new Cause-5 code is needed.
5.3 Review-checklist pass (RESPONSE.md): no PROD command ran without permission;
    exhibit worktrees untouched; recount recorded before any victory claim.

Gate: `BASELINE.md` present and self-contained — a stranger can re-run the
whole proof from the kit + this file alone.

## Validation & assurance plan (how we know it worked)

No unit tests by design (ops task — RESPONSE.md S5: "No new unit tests;
deliverable is the recount + version record"). Assurance instead comes from
executed procedures with saved evidence, each claim cross-checked two ways:

| Claim | Primary evidence | Independent cross-check |
|---|---|---|
| Runners on fix build | `GET /runners` version facts | `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0` + heartbeat build fields |
| Bare → ~0 | Fleet script `bare` count post-converge | Reason-vocabulary audit (1.3): every new interrupt carries a reason naming a cause |
| No commit crash-loops | FAILED + `gitFailure` completions, no interrupt row | Journal: single `commit failed` per incident, no restart storm |
| E5 classification | Worktree stage-output-commit presence | Journal `Runner failed:` line + origin SHA check |
| No server-restart orphans | `server_restart` count stays 0 | Backend build/`engine.updatedAt` divergence log (Cause-6 upkeep) |

Per-phase gates above double as the test plan: a phase is done only when its
artifact file exists with the named content. Negative controls: (a) BEFORE
snapshot must show still-bare new interrupts (proves the premise that 0.1.0
emits no reasons); (b) any reasoned non-cap interrupt pre-converge, or any
bare interrupt post-converge, fails its gate and must be explained, not
averaged away. Docs assurance: every record file carries timestamps, raw
command output (or the raw JSON), and the exact re-run command.

## Deliverables (all under `docs/tasks/683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c/`)

- `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` (this file) · `SURVEY.md` (prior stage, read-only
  input) · `RUN-LOG.md` · `bin/fleet-recount.sh` · `bin/runners-snapshot.sh` ·
  `bin/e5-sweep.sh` · `runners-before/*.json` + `runners-after/*.json` ·
  `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md` · `RECOUNT-AFTER.md` · `E5-SWEEP.md` · `BASELINE.md`.

## Risks & non-goals

- Convergence may take >24 h per runner (daily nudge, idle-only). Mitigation:
  q3 default waits in-run; q3-fallback splits BEFORE/Phase 2 now, AFTER later.
- S1/S2/S4/S6 landing mid-window confounds attribution. Mitigation: confound
  ledger + per-runner converge-time gating (§Approach).
- E5 exhibits already thinning (all four seeds absent on server2-alpha).
  Mitigation: sweep early (Phase 2), sibling host + origin + journal fallbacks,
  explicit gap notes.
- Access refusal (q2-fallbacks). Mitigation: degraded-scope branches per survey
  row; procedure-only doc as last resort.
- Non-goals: no runner/backend code, no knob change under the default
  assumption, no restarts/updates/reaps/re-runs, no Cause-5 ticket unless 2.4
  triggers, no claiming S1/S2/S4/S6 signals as S5 wins.

## Open questions

1. SURVEY.md q1–q4 unanswered — plan proceeds on recommended-option assumptions
   (table above); execution re-checks for answers first.
2. RESPONSE_SURVEY.md q1–q9 unanswered, including q9 (rollout pace) — q9's
   recommended option is treated as a hard constraint regardless.
3. Live `runnerRecommendedVersion` value — read-only check in 0.3 decides
   whether the rollout is already switched on.
4. Whether any E5 seed worktree survives on the local-alpha host — answered by
   the first sweep in Phase 2.
5. q4-fallback needs the full project list if "all projects" is chosen —
   enumerate via `GET /tasks` without project filter at that point.

## Sources (all inspected in-branch or in-checkout this run)

- `kb/2e663986` branch: `RESPONSE.md` (S5 + blocking map + checklist),
  `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` (§2 table, Causes 1–6, amplifier, E1–E7 matrix, §6
  method), `GUIDE-05-commit-push-crash-loop.md` (§4 E5 sweep),
  `GUIDE-07-amplifier-requeue-and-display.md` (§5 fleet script),
  `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` (q9), `TDD-TEST-EXAMPLES.md` (safety tiers),
  `REPLICATION-INDEX.md`, `TICKETS-CREATED-20261122.md` (API base, project).
- `origin/kb/683f0bfd` branch: `SURVEY.md` (q1–q4, unanswered),
  `idea-20261122-181543.md` (Idea approval).
- Checkout: `docs/runner-update-runbook.md` (release/nudge/triage),
  `runner/version.json` (0.2.0), `api/config/schema.js:424-432` (knob
  defaults), `api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:457` (`GET /runners`),
  tags `runner-v0.1.0`/`runner-v0.2.0`, commits `046a6391`/`f430f53`/`7ac148ce`.

reports.content:
# REVIEW — S5 stage review of `kb/683f0bfd` work products (PR-review stage, docs-only)

Task: `683f0bfd-9132-41e1-b468-2cb8c428e08c` (RESPONSE.md S5 of `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4`).
Reviewer: review stage, 2026-11-23T10:46:33Z. Read-only against prod (GET /runners, GET /deploy/status,
GET /tasks fixtures already on disk); no runner/backend writes, no restarts, no reaps (q9 held).
Sources re-read: `RESPONSE.md` S5, `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md` §2 + Cause 5, `GUIDE-05` §4,
`GUIDE-07` §5, `RESPONSE_SURVEY.md` q9, `docs/runner-update-runbook.md`, this folder's
`IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` / `SURVEY.md` / `bin/` / `raw/` / `runners-before/` / `recount-before-*`,
and the repo code/git (`runner-v0.2.0` tag, `046a6391`, `7ac148ce`, `api/config/schema.js`,
`api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js`).

## Verdict summary

**FAIL — needs more work before integrate.** The observe-only BEFORE evidence is good and the
premise still holds (0.1.0 runners emit no non-cap reasons), but (a) the task's central premise
is falsified: the only published 0.2.x release, tag `runner-v0.2.0`, does **not** contain the
fix `046a6391`, and the live backend still recommends `0.1.0`, so no runner can converge to a
fix-bearing build in the current state; (b) the test suite that is supposed to pin the ops kit
is broken and never reaches its e2e tests; (c) the plan's named deliverables are missing and one
evidence sweep (server2) is an unexplained empty file.

## Review questions

| Question | Answer |
|---|---|
| Achieves the goal (converge runners to a build with `046a6391` + before/after recount)? | **No.** Only the BEFORE half exists (`runners-after/` empty). Convergence is currently impossible — see F1/F2. |
| Followed the plan? | Partially: Phase 0–2 executed (kit, before snapshot, before recount, local E5 sweep). Phases 3–5 not done; plan deliverables `RUN-LOG.md`, `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md`, `BASELINE.md` absent. Survey q1 answer ("knob already set") is contradicted by live data and never reconciled. |
| Code standards? | Ops scripts: yes (fail-loud, atomic writes, validated task ids, read-only probes, no secrets). Test suite: **no** — F3. |
| Easy to modify later? | Yes — modular `bin/jq/*`, env overrides, mock API. |
| Best practices? | Mostly; E5 classification grep is not task-scoped (F5); empty server2 sweep has no gap note (F4). |
| Unnecessary tech debt? | Minor: two e5 worklist files in different shapes; before artifacts produced by an older script revision (no `recount-before-meta.json`/`-errors.jsonl`). |
| Docs updated? | `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` + `SURVEY.md` present, but the plan's "grounded facts" are wrong (F1/F2) and the narrative records are missing (F4). |

## Findings

### F1 (blocker — premise falsified) — `runner-v0.2.0` does NOT contain the fix

- `git rev-parse runner-v0.2.0^{commit}` → `8460e4a83f6664bcdd353b7307cfd03da7149d6f`, dated
  **2026-11-19 22:47:45Z**. The fix `046a6391` was merged **2026-11-21 09:38:57Z** in `7ac148ce`.
- `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0^{commit}` → **rc=1 (NO)** — the plan's own
  success criterion 1 check fails.
- `git show runner-v0.2.0:shared/gitFailure.js` → "exists on disk, but not in runner-v0.2.0";
  the generic catch in `runner-v0.2.0:runner/daemon.js` attaches **no** interrupt reason
  (only the workdir-cap path does). At HEAD the generic catch sends `interruptReason` and the
  `gitFailure` branch exists (`runner/daemon.js:2366-2374`, `:2441-2447`).
- Consequence: the plan's grounded fact "release tags `runner-v0.1.0` AND `runner-v0.2.0` both
  exist, so the 0.2.x release is already cut (runbook step 4 done)" conflates tag existence with
  tag content. Converging runners to the published `0.2.0` would still leave them without
  reasons and without deterministic-git-failure handling — bare interrupts would persist.
- Required (PROD-ACTION, outside this docs-only task, record as blocking prerequisite): cut a
  **new** release (e.g. `runner-v0.2.1`) from a commit ≥ `7ac148ce` per runbook ("never move an
  existing tag"), then raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (runbook step 5).

### F2 (blocker — live rollout state) — knob still 0.1.0, no nudge pending

Read-only `GET http://192.168.1.206:3100/runners` at **2026-11-23T10:36:57Z** (saved as
`runners-review/runners-20261123T103657Z.{json,tsv}`):

- All active runners (`local-alpha`, `local-bravo`, `server2-alpha`) report `runnerVersion 0.1.0`;
  `recommendedVersion 0.1.0`; `availableVersions ["0.1.0"]`; `updateAvailable false`;
  `pendingCommands []` — **no update nudge is even pending**.
- `availableVersions` = runner-reported versions + recommended/minimum knobs only
  (`api/flow/runnerVersionCompat.js:224-244` `fleetKnownVersions`), so `["0.1.0"]` confirms the
  live `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` is still `0.1.0` (`api/config/schema.js:425-432`
  default). This contradicts `SURVEY.md` q1's answer ("already set — observe only"); no record
  in the folder reconciles the two.
- `local-alpha`/`local-bravo` build sha `fbcf8442ee031e2edbc9f0b30195afa410296cf3`
  (built 2026-11-14): `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 fbcf8442…` → **NO**.
  `server2-alpha` reports **no build sha** — by design the snapshot verdict must say
  "cannot verify", never converged.
- Backend build: `GET /deploy/status` → build 637, deployed 2026-11-21T22:00:17Z,
  headSha `7ac148ce…` (backend has the fix; runners don't).
- Consequence: q3's "wait until both converge, then after-recount in the same run" cannot
  complete in this state. The task must either wait on F1's prerequisite (human PROD-ACTION) or
  switch to the q3-fallback (deliver BEFORE + E5 now, AFTER as a scheduled follow-up) — and say
  so explicitly in `RUN-LOG.md`.

### F3 (verification broken) — `bin/tests/run-tests.sh` does not pass as committed

Re-ran the suite at ~2026-11-23T10:40Z (log captured in the session; nothing written outside
`$WORK` temp):

- T1–T5, T7, T8 **pass** (incl. T1: current `jq/per-task.jq` + `jq/aggregate.jq` over all 81
  `raw/before/*.json` fixtures reproduce `recount-before-table.json` exactly, and T6 ancestry:
  HEAD contains fix → true, `runner-v0.2.0` lacks fix → false).
- **T6 verdict checks FAIL ×4**: `mk_runner()` (run-tests.sh ~line 132) has an extra closing
  brace — `…build: (if $sha == "" then null else {sha: $sha} end)}}}}` → jq 1.8.1 syntax error
  at column 194 — so all four `runner-verdict.jq` assertions receive empty input and FAIL.
- Suite then **aborts at line 191**: `MOCK_BADJSON_ID: unbound variable` — `VAR=… start_mock …`
  prefix assignments do not persist after the function call under bash 5.3 + `set -u`, so the
  next line's `$MOCK_BADJSON_ID` is unbound; `set -e` kills the script. **T9-badjson, T10
  (fleet-recount e2e), T11 (runners-snapshot e2e), T12 never execute and no `RESULT:` line is
  printed.** The header comment's claim "pinned by bin/tests/run-tests.sh" is therefore
  unproven for everything past T9, and no test-result artifact is stored in the folder.

### F4 (deliverables / evidence gaps)

- `runners-after/` is empty; `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md`, `RUN-LOG.md`, `BASELINE.md`
  (named in the plan's Deliverables) do not exist — only raw artifacts.
- `raw/e5-sweep-server2-before.txt` is **0 bytes** with no evidence-gap note. The server2 host
  is where the 413/502 journal evidence lives (WIDE_NET Cause 2/4); the local-only sweep
  cannot substitute for it. Record the gap explicitly or re-run when server2 ssh works.
- `recount-before-meta.json` / `recount-before-errors.jsonl` absent — the before artifacts were
  produced by an earlier script revision (`raw/recount-before-stderr.txt` format ≠ current
  `fleet-recount.sh` log format). T1 passing mitigates this for the numbers; still, re-run the
  before with the frozen kit (or note why not).
- `raw/e5-worklist-before.json` (flat `{task,ts,runner,delta}` rows) differs in shape from
  `recount-before-e5worklist.json` (grouped by task, 19 entries) — duplicate worklists, no note
  which is canonical.
- `runners-before/` has no `verdict-*.txt/json` — `runners-snapshot.sh` writes them, so the
  before snapshot predates the verdict feature.

### F5 (minor, classification accuracy) — e5-sweep stage-output grep is not task-scoped

`bin/e5-sweep.sh` detects a stage-output commit via `git log --format=%s -20 … | grep -qi
"stage output"` without matching the task's own branch. On mirror/merged history the last 20
subjects can belong to other tasks — observed in `raw/e5-sweep-before.txt`, where the origin
listing under `kb/7f6220c3-…` shows `kb/1cae113f-…` stage-output commits. A false "PRESENT"
would flip a verdict to Cause 2/4. Fix: match `^kb/$PREFIX.*stage output` (or check the ref tip).

### F6 (positives — what holds)

- Observe-only discipline held throughout: no restarts/updates/reaps/re-runs; all prod access
  was read-only GETs (q2/q9).
- Negative control holds: `recount-before-table.json` (81 tasks, project
  `0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a`, fetched 2026-11-23T09:04Z) — 145 runner interrupts,
  70 with reason, 75 bare; `reason_vocabulary` contains **only** workdir-cap strings → 0.1.0
  still emits no non-cap reasons. A fresh bare post-`finished` interrupt still accrued on
  0.1.0 runners this morning (`3b82f6ae`, 2026-11-23T08:25:23Z, server2-alpha) — premise
  re-confirmed.
- Local E5 journal evidence (`raw/e5-sweep-before.txt`) shows MERGE_CONFLICT
  ("refusing to resolve on the push path") and binary-guard HOOK_REJECTED ("recovery:
  unpushed work … failed") — both deterministic classes that `046a6391` covers
  (`HOOK_REJECTED`/`COMMIT_FAILED`/`MERGE_CONFLICT`). Per RESPONSE.md S5 step 3, current
  evidence does **not** trigger a new Cause-5 code ticket.
- Kit design is good: fail-loud helpers, atomic evidence writes, JSON validation on GET, task-id
  injection guard, base64-encoded remote probe, password never in argv/logs.

## Required fixes before this stage can pass

1. **F1/F2**: correct `IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` grounded facts (tag content ≠ HEAD); record the
   merge-base proof and the live knob state (2026-11-23T10:36:57Z snapshot in `runners-review/`);
   add a blocking prerequisite entry: new runner release cut from ≥ `7ac148ce` (e.g.
   `runner-v0.2.1`, never move `runner-v0.2.0`) + `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` raise —
   both PROD-ACTION for a human; until then adopt the q3-fallback (BEFORE + E5 now, AFTER later)
   in `RUN-LOG.md`.
2. **F3**: fix `bin/tests/run-tests.sh` — remove the extra `}` in `mk_runner()`; hoist
   `MOCK_BADJSON_ID` / `MOCK_FAIL_IDS` / `MOCK_EMPTY` / `R_FILE` to plain assignments before the
   `start_mock` calls; re-run to `RESULT: N passed, 0 failed` and store the log under `raw/`.
3. **F4**: write `RUN-LOG.md`, `RECOUNT-BEFORE.md`, `E5-SWEEP.md` from the raw artifacts; mark the
   empty server2 sweep as an explicit evidence gap (or re-run it); designate one canonical e5
   worklist; re-run `runners-snapshot.sh` so `verdict-*` files exist for the before snapshot.
4. **F5**: scope the stage-output grep in `bin/e5-sweep.sh` to `kb/$PREFIX` and add a T7 pin for
   the cross-task false-positive case.

## Evidence index (this review)

- `runners-review/runners-20261123T103657Z.json` / `.tsv` — read-only `GET /runners` at review time.
- Git: `runner-v0.2.0^{commit}` = `8460e4a8` (2026-11-19); `046a6391` merged 2026-11-21 09:38 in
  `7ac148ce`; `git merge-base --is-ancestor 046a6391 runner-v0.2.0^{commit}` → rc=1;
  `git show runner-v0.2.0:shared/gitFailure.js` → absent; live build `fbcf8442…` lacks the fix.
- API: `GET /deploy/status` build 637 (headSha `7ac148ce…`) at 2026-11-23T10:37Z.
- Tests: `bash bin/tests/run-tests.sh` → T6 ×4 FAIL (mk_runner jq syntax error), abort at line
  191 (`MOCK_BADJSON_ID` unbound), T10–T12 never run, no RESULT line.

# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS — high level of task interruptions

Task: `2e663986-aaf3-4afe-8dcf-3adad34acdb4` ("noticing a high level of interruptions").
Date: 2026-11-21. Stage: DO research (investigatory only — no solutions proposed).

## 0. Inputs

- **Bug report**: many tasks end with interruptions suggesting flakiness; reporter
  notes a `local-alpha` runner restart-loop incident and wonders if it is related;
  interruptions "should happen rarely but they are seemingly quite common".
- **Screenshot** (`assets/image.png`): task `7f6220c3` ("add support for projects
  having the kainbain docs in a seperate repo") showing repeated
  "Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue" rows and high
  "Tried N times" counts (Merge resolver ×6, Quick review ×6, Automated
  tests ×10, In Progress ×11).
- **Survey result**: the Questionnaire stage recorded `Survey completed (none)` —
  the `question-me` skill requested no survey questions, so there is no
  `SURVEY.md` with human answers. All evidence below comes from repo code,
  the live backend API, runner worktrees, and the runner systemd journal.

## 1. How interruptions work (mechanics primer)

Two code paths flip a task to `interrupted` (verified by repo search):

1. **Server-restart path** — `reconcileInterruptedRuns`
   (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`): at boot, any task left in
   `running_agent` / `running_ci` / `running_merge` / `advancing` (see
   `ORPHANED_RUNNING_STATUSES` in `api/flow/scheduler/orphanedRunningStatuses.js`)
   with no engine owner becomes `interrupted`, history
   `Stage execution interrupted by server restart`.
2. **Runner path** — `POST /tasks/:id/interrupt` (`api/flow/runnerRoutes.js:1067`)
   → `executionLedger.interruptExecution` (`api/flow/executionLedger.js:608`):

Section 4 of `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md`. Not a root cause, but it turns each
interrupt into the screenshot's "quite common" impression (`assets/image.png`)
and into parked tasks.

- **Verdict: REPLICABLE-LOCALLY** (api + frontend unit tests).
- **Code seams:** `api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js` (single history
  string `Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue` for BOTH
  recovery routes); `api/flow/scheduler/scheduleTick.js:178-181` (interrupted
  candidate is auto-resumed and dispatched in the same tick — no backoff);
  `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.js` (Rule-0: oldest interruption
  first); `api/flow/executionLedger.js` `interruptExecution` (increments
  `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally — cap refusals count as deaths, see
  GUIDE 01); `frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:483-536`
  (`summarizeStageRuns` sets `tryCount` = grouped row count, capped at
  `STAGE_RUN_TRY_COUNT_CAP = 99` at `:461`) and `:556` (`formatTryCount` ->
  `Tried {n} times`).

## 1. Signature (recognise it)

- `assets/image.png`: every stage row shows "Auto-resumed after server
  restart — prioritised in queue" and a high "Tried N times" badge, while
  backend history shows **zero** actual server-restart interrupts.
- Interrupt -> resume -> re-claim cadence of ~150 ms–60 s with no backoff.

## 2. Safe local tests — the mislabel (api, vitest)

Pin that a runner-path interrupt (no server restart happened) is resumed
under the "server restart" label. Existing harness: `api/flow/taskScheduler.test.js:896`
(`describe("autoResumeTask")`). Proposed additions (code stage):
`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js`

```js
import { describe, test, expect } from "vitest";
import { autoResumeTask } from "./autoResumeTask.js";
// mock store as in api/flow/taskScheduler.test.js:896

test("PIN current behaviour: a runner-path interrupt resumes under the 'server restart' label", () => {
  store.tasks["t-1"].status = "interrupted"; // set by executionLedger.interruptExecution (runner path)
  autoResumeTask(store, "p-1", "t-1", "/repo");
  const actions = store.tasks["t-1"].history.map((h) => h.action);
  expect(actions).toContain("Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue");
});

test("TDD red-test for the fix: runner-path resumes must NOT claim a server restart", () => {
  store.tasks["t-1"].status = "interrupted";
  store.tasks["t-1"].interruptedBy = "runner:local-alpha"; // set by interruptExecution
  autoResumeTask(store, "p-1", "t-1", "/repo");
  const actions = store.tasks["t-1"].history.map((h) => h.action);
  expect(actions.some((a) => a.includes("server restart"))).toBe(false); // FAILS today -> red
  expect(actions.some((a) => a.includes("Auto-resumed"))).toBe(true);
});
```

Run: `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js`

## 3. Safe local tests — Rule-0 instant pickup, no backoff (api, vitest)

Proposed `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js`: with one
fresh `in_stage` task and one `interrupted` task (or one carrying
`resumedAfterInterruption`), assert `findResumedCandidate(store)` returns the
interrupted one with `priorityReason: "resumed_interrupted"`, and that
`scheduleTick` dispatches it in the same tick (see `scheduleTick.js:178-181`).
TDD red-test for a backoff fix: after N consecutive resumes of the same
task+stage, the resumed candidate should sort behind fresh work —
`expect(candidate.taskId).toBe("t-fresh")` fails today.

## 4. Safe local tests — "Tried N times" inflation (frontend, vitest)

`summarizeStageRuns` counts every grouped timeline row — `Advanced`, `Moved`,
`Failed`, and every `Resumed` row (each auto-resume writes one) — into
`tryCount`. Reproduce the screenshot's x6/x10/x11 badges. Proposed additions
to `frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.test.js`
(see its `describe('summarizeStageRuns')` at :1254):

```js
it('PIN: interrupt/resume cycles inflate tryCount (screenshot badges)', () => {
  const entries = [
    { stage: 'In Progress', status: 'Resumed', timestamp: 't5' },
    { stage: 'In Progress', status: 'Failed', timestamp: 't4', reason: 'x' },
    { stage: 'In Progress', status: 'Resumed', timestamp: 't3' },
    { stage: 'In Progress', status: 'Resumed', timestamp: 't2' },
    { stage: 'In Progress', status: 'Advanced', timestamp: 't1' },
  ];
  const [row] = summarizeStageRuns(entries, []);
  expect(row.tryCount).toBe(5);
  expect(formatTryCount(row)).toBe('Tried 5 times');
});

it('TDD red-test for the fix: Resumed rows are re-tries of infra, not stage attempts', () => {
  const entries = [ /* same as above */ ];
  const [row] = summarizeStageRuns(entries, []);
  expect(row.tryCount).toBe(2); // Advanced + Failed only — FAILS today (currently 5)
});
```

```bash
curl -s 'http://192.168.1.206:3100/tasks?projectId=0fd41821' | jq -r '.[].id' | while read t; do

        server_restart: map(select(test("interrupted by server restart"))) | length,
        escalated: map(select(test("Runner deaths escalated"))) | length

done
```

# GUIDE 07 — Amplifier: instant re-queue + display mechanics multiply every flake

Section 4 of `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md`. Not a root cause, but it turns each
interrupt into the screenshot's "quite common" impression (`assets/image.png`)
and into parked tasks.

- **Verdict: REPLICABLE-LOCALLY** (api + frontend unit tests).
- **Code seams:** `api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeTask.js` (single history
  string `Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue` for BOTH
  recovery routes); `api/flow/scheduler/scheduleTick.js:178-181` (interrupted
  candidate is auto-resumed and dispatched in the same tick — no backoff);
  `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.js` (Rule-0: oldest interruption
  first); `api/flow/executionLedger.js` `interruptExecution` (increments
  `runnerInterruptCount` unconditionally — cap refusals count as deaths, see
  GUIDE 01); `frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.js:483-536`
  (`summarizeStageRuns` sets `tryCount` = grouped row count, capped at
  `STAGE_RUN_TRY_COUNT_CAP = 99` at `:461`) and `:556` (`formatTryCount` ->
  `Tried {n} times`).

## 1. Signature (recognise it)

- `assets/image.png`: every stage row shows "Auto-resumed after server
  restart — prioritised in queue" and a high "Tried N times" badge, while
  backend history shows **zero** actual server-restart interrupts.
- Interrupt -> resume -> re-claim cadence of ~150 ms–60 s with no backoff.

## 2. Safe local tests — the mislabel (api, vitest)

Pin that a runner-path interrupt (no server restart happened) is resumed
under the "server restart" label. Existing harness: `api/flow/taskScheduler.test.js:896`
(`describe("autoResumeTask")`). Proposed additions (code stage):
`api/flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js`

```js
import { describe, test, expect } from "vitest";
import { autoResumeTask } from "./autoResumeTask.js";
// mock store as in api/flow/taskScheduler.test.js:896

test("PIN current behaviour: a runner-path interrupt resumes under the 'server restart' label", () => {
  store.tasks["t-1"].status = "interrupted"; // set by executionLedger.interruptExecution (runner path)
  autoResumeTask(store, "p-1", "t-1", "/repo");
  const actions = store.tasks["t-1"].history.map((h) => h.action);
  expect(actions).toContain("Auto-resumed after server restart — prioritised in queue");
});

test("TDD red-test for the fix: runner-path resumes must NOT claim a server restart", () => {
  store.tasks["t-1"].status = "interrupted";
  store.tasks["t-1"].interruptedBy = "runner:local-alpha"; // set by interruptExecution
  autoResumeTask(store, "p-1", "t-1", "/repo");
  const actions = store.tasks["t-1"].history.map((h) => h.action);
  expect(actions.some((a) => a.includes("server restart"))).toBe(false); // FAILS today -> red
  expect(actions.some((a) => a.includes("Auto-resumed"))).toBe(true);
});
```

Run: `cd api && npx vitest run flow/scheduler/autoResumeLabel.test.js`

## 3. Safe local tests — Rule-0 instant pickup, no backoff (api, vitest)

Proposed `api/flow/scheduler/findResumedCandidate.priority.test.js`: with one
fresh `in_stage` task and one `interrupted` task (or one carrying
`resumedAfterInterruption`), assert `findResumedCandidate(store)` returns the
interrupted one with `priorityReason: "resumed_interrupted"`, and that
`scheduleTick` dispatches it in the same tick (see `scheduleTick.js:178-181`).
TDD red-test for a backoff fix: after N consecutive resumes of the same
task+stage, the resumed candidate should sort behind fresh work —
`expect(candidate.taskId).toBe("t-fresh")` fails today.

## 4. Safe local tests — "Tried N times" inflation (frontend, vitest)

`summarizeStageRuns` counts every grouped timeline row — `Advanced`, `Moved`,
`Failed`, and every `Resumed` row (each auto-resume writes one) — into
`tryCount`. Reproduce the screenshot's x6/x10/x11 badges. Proposed additions
to `frontend/src/components/tasks/taskFormatters.test.js`
(see its `describe('summarizeStageRuns')` at :1254):

```js
it('PIN: interrupt/resume cycles inflate tryCount (screenshot badges)', () => {
  const entries = [
    { stage: 'In Progress', status: 'Resumed', timestamp: 't5' },
    { stage: 'In Progress', status: 'Failed', timestamp: 't4', reason: 'x' },
    { stage: 'In Progress', status: 'Resumed', timestamp: 't3' },
    { stage: 'In Progress', status: 'Resumed', timestamp: 't2' },
    { stage: 'In Progress', status: 'Advanced', timestamp: 't1' },
  ];
  const [row] = summarizeStageRuns(entries, []);
  expect(row.tryCount).toBe(5);
  expect(formatTryCount(row)).toBe('Tried 5 times');
});

it('TDD red-test for the fix: Resumed rows are re-tries of infra, not stage attempts', () => {
  const entries = [ /* same as above */ ];
  const [row] = summarizeStageRuns(entries, []);
  expect(row.tryCount).toBe(2); // Advanced + Failed only — FAILS today (currently 5)
});
```

## 5. Prod-only verification

`PROD-ONLY — DO NOT RUN WITHOUT EXPLICIT USER PERMISSION` (read-only API) — the
fleet-wide counts behind the amplifier (re-run after the 0.2.x runner rollout
as the before/after test):

```bash
curl -s 'http://192.168.1.206:3100/tasks?projectId=0fd41821' | jq -r '.[].id' | while read t; do
  curl -s "http://192.168.1.206:3100/tasks/$t?projectId=0fd41821" \
    | jq -r --arg t "$t" '[.history[]?.action] | {
        task: $t,

        server_restart: map(select(test("interrupted by server restart"))) | length,
        escalated: map(select(test("Runner deaths escalated"))) | length
      } | @json';
done
```

## 6. Evidence to collect

- Per-task counts from §5 (before/after runner rollout).
- UI rows (`assets/image.png` pattern) mapped to the same task's history —
  showing Resumed rows counted into "Tried N times" and runner-path resumes
  labelled "after server restart".

### Cause 1 — Worktree-capacity exhaustion loop (`WORKTREE_CAP_REACHED`, cap ~5)

**Summary.** The runner refuses new work when its work-root holds ~5 live/orphan
workdirs and none are stale enough to evict; it reports an interrupt with a
reason and keeps polling (`runner/daemon.js:2299-2314`). The task re-queues with
Rule-0 priority and is immediately re-claimed — often by the same still-full
runner — producing a tight interrupt/resume cycle. Each refusal also increments
the runner-death counter, so a capacity problem eventually parks the task as a
suspected death loop.

**Pros (for).**
- Direct textual evidence: all 49 reasoned interrupts (41% of the fleet total)
  carry `Reason: Runner workdir unavailable: Worktree cap reached (~5); ...
  (every orphan was used recently, nothing stale to evict)`. Both hosts appear
  (`/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` = local-alpha host, `/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain` =
  server2-alpha host).
- Timing fits: cap refusal happens inside `prepareWorkdir`, seconds after
  `started` — matching the dominant ≤15s bucket.
- Code path returns (no crash) and keeps polling, which explains rapid
  re-claim cycles without process restarts.
- Crash loops (Causes 2–4) leave orphan workdirs behind (observed: 5 orphans
  listed at every server2-alpha boot on 11-20), so this cause is also a
  second-order effect of the other causes — they feed each other.

**Cons (against).**
- Explains at most 49/118 interrupts; the 69 bare interrupts cannot be cap
  refusals on the deployed builds (both runners demonstrably emit the cap
  reason since the 10-29/11-11 build, and reasoned cap interrupts appear on
  both hosts).
- Does not explain the ≥2min post-`finished` interrupts (15 cases).
- Reasoned cap interrupts cluster 11-09 → 11-17; the 11-19/11-20 spike
  (48 bare) needs a different driver.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `350ca162` (12 cap interrupts), `db24c124` (9), `7b69d365` (6), `3c12ffcd`
  (5), `f56e9878` (4), `1f8959ca` (5) — confirm each shows the cap reason and
  same-runner re-claim.
- Runner-side: work-root occupancy time series per host around 11-09 and
  11-16/17; orphan-staleness / LRU-eviction decisions in daemon logs.
- Backend: `GET /tasks/<id>` history for `WORKTREE_CAP` reason strings is the
  cheapest ongoing detector (no host access needed).

### Cause 2 — Completion report rejected with HTTP 413 (payload > Fastify 1 MiB default)

**Summary.** After a fully successful agent run + `commitAndPush`
(commit AND push succeed), the runner's `complete-execution` POST exceeds the
backend JSON body limit and is rejected with 413. The daemon's generic catch
(`runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`, deployed 0.1.0 without reason attachment) reports
a bare interrupt and rethrows → `exit(1)` → systemd restart → re-claim → the
agent re-runs for minutes → commit+push again → 413 again. Deterministic loop;
each lap is recorded as one interruption + auto-resume and burns a full stage
run. The 413 trigger on the observed task is `collectTaskFiles`
(`runner/daemon.js:1820` / deployed `daemon.js:1346`): top-level task-doc files
up to ~1 MiB total — and this task's folder holds 2.8 MiB including many
top-level PNG screenshots each under the 256 KiB per-file cap — plus the 20 KiB
output and JSON envelope, against Fastify's default 1 MiB limit
(`api/index.js:116` sets no `bodyLimit`; the only explicit `bodyLimit` in the
API is the accessibility route).

**Pros (for).**
- Smoking gun in the server2-alpha journal (`journalctl --user
  -u kainbain-runner-server2-alpha`): on 11-20, five consecutive cycles of
  `Committed <sha> (pushed: true)` → `Runner failed: Backend 413 on
  /tasks/7f6220c3-.../complete-execution` → `Main process exited, status=1`
  → `Scheduled restart job, restart counter 830→834`, at 21:19, 21:29, 21:35,
  21:43, 21:47 — exactly matching the five `finished` → bare-interrupt pairs
  in task `7f6220c3` history.
- Worktree forensics agree: `kb-7f6220c3` holds the pushed stage-output commits
  with matching timestamps, and `origin` has them — proving failure happened
  strictly after push.
- Deterministic: same task files every lap → same 413 → loop only ends via the
  death-bound park (observed: parked at count 7).
- Explains why the newest, longest, most asset-heavy stages (Merge resolver
  with proof screenshots) interrupt while short stages complete.

**Cons (against).**
- Proven for exactly one task-stage so far (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver, 5
  interrupts); the other 10 post-`finished` bare interrupts are unexamined.
- Cannot explain the 99 sub-15s interrupts (413 only happens at completion,
  minutes in).
- Backend 413 leaves no task-history trace of its own (the backend rejects
  before routing), so backend history alone can never confirm/deny further
  cases — runner journals are required.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `7f6220c3` (screenshot task; Merge-resolver window 11-20 21:15–21:47):
  backend access/error log for the five 413s (confirm size vs limit);
  preserve `kb-7f6220c3` worktree (do not reap) — 2.8 MiB task-docs exhibit.
- Journal sweep on both runner hosts for `Backend 413` across all tasks/dates
  (server2-alpha: 5 hits since 11-19, all this task; local-alpha journal still
  needed — host `192.168.1.206`, user `server`).
- Any other task whose `finished` → interrupt gap is seconds with a preceding
  multi-minute run is a 413 suspect; check runner journals first, backend
  history second (it will be bare).

### Cause 3 — local-alpha premature-death loop in worktree setup (bare, ~5s, no `prompted`)

**Summary.** The volume-dominant signature: `local-alpha` claims a task
(`started`), then ~5–11s later reports a bare interrupt without ever emitting
`prompted` — i.e. it dies inside `prepareWorkdir` (git fetch/worktree-add,
residue handling, LRU eviction, docs worktree) or the process dies there — then
re-claims ~20–60s later and repeats until the death bound parks the task. This
matches the reporter's "local-alpha restart loop" incident. The underlying fault
is unknown precisely because the deployed 0.1.0 build attaches no reason on the
generic path (reason support landed 11-21 in `046a6391`, after these events).

**Pros (for).**
- Dominant by volume: 96/118 interrupts are local-alpha; 99/118 fleet-wide fall
  in the ≤15s bucket (median 4.7s); the bare-by-day spike is 11-19 (30) and
  11-20 (18).
- Two textbook exhibits: `c5c465c4` — 28 bare local-alpha interrupts ~18s apart
  on 11-19 12:15–12:37; `7f6220c3` — In-Progress loop (11-20 15:38–15:43, ×5 to
  escalation), Quick-review loop (18:39–18:41, ×4), plus 10:16 and 13:34
  single-shot deaths on 11-21 seconds after a manual resume.
- Localisation is tight: no `prompted` ⇒ pre-harness ⇒ `prepareWorkdir` region
  (only uncaught fallible step there).
- The deployed build cannot exonerate or name the fault (no reason), so "bare +
  fast + local" is exactly what any setup-phase fault looks like on 0.1.0.

**Cons (against).**

meta.output:
**Cons (against).**
- Root fault genuinely unidentified — could be git (lock/fetch/push-race),
  disk, permissions, docs-worktree handling (note: `7f6220c3` IS the
  separate-docs-repo task, and stage output mentions docs worktrees), a stale
  mirror, or backend-call failures during setup. No evidence yet discriminates.
- Cycle period varies (~18s on `c5c465c4` vs ~40–60s on `7f6220c3`), suggesting
  possibly two sub-mechanisms (in-process re-claim vs systemd restart); local
  restart counters are unknown from here.
- "Restart loop" implies process restarts, but a tight claim→interrupt→re-claim
  cycle without restarts would look identical in backend history.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `c5c465c4` (28×, 11-19 12:15–12:37), `7f6220c3` (In Progress 11-20
  15:38–15:43; Quick review 18:39–18:41; 11-21 10:16 + 13:34), `350ca162`
  (12× local) — need the **local-alpha daemon journal on the backend host**
  (`192.168.1.206`, `~server`, systemd user unit) for those windows: the
  `Runner failed: <message>` line names the fault, and restart-counter lines
  separate crash-loops from re-claim loops.
- local-alpha build provenance: confirm it is also pre-11-21 (expected bare);
  after the 0.2.x rollout, bare interrupts should vanish and reasons should
  name this cause directly — re-run the §2 counts as the before/after test.
- Work-root/disk/git-mirror health on the backend host at those times.

### Cause 4 — Backend-unreachable / 502 windows crashing the daemon mid-run

**Summary.** The runner daemon treats backend call failures as fatal: `fetch
failed` (undici network error) and `Backend 502` crash the process (`exit(1)` →
systemd restart). When the failure lands inside an assignment (claim, logs,
progress, complete, heartbeat/renewal handling), the generic catch reports an
interrupt (bare on 0.1.0) and the restart cycle begins. server2-alpha is a
remote runner over LAN, so it is exposed to every network blip and every
backend restart/502 window.

**Pros (for).**
- server2-alpha journal since 11-19: 501 × `fetch failed` and 16 × `Backend
  502` (`/runners/heartbeat`, `/runners/dispatch`); the idle-loop sample
  (11-19 11:15:20–11:15:44) shows three consecutive `fetch failed` crashes with
  restart counters 366→367 — proving the daemon exits rather than retries.
- A proven backend 502 window on 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 (seven heartbeat 502s,
  new pid each ~6s) coincides with backend build 637 `deployedAt`
  2026-11-20T20:40:14Z and `engine.updatedAt` 20:40:57Z — i.e. a real backend
  restart/downtime window, observed from the runner side.
- Any in-flight assignment spanning such a window (or a LAN blip) on the 0.1.0
  build becomes a bare interrupt — consistent with scattered bare interrupts on
  both runners.

**Cons (against).**
- The 11-20 20:40 backend restart demonstrably did NOT interrupt the in-flight
  Quick-review stage on `7f6220c3` (it completed 20:44:48), so heartbeat/502
  windows are survivable mid-run at least sometimes — the fatality depends on
  which call fails (fatal inside `executeAssignment`'s try, tolerated in the
  renewal/heartbeat path).
- No bare interrupt has yet been timestamp-matched to a specific 502/fetch-fail
  crash mid-assignment; the 501 `fetch failed` lines are dominated by idle-loop
  polls with no task impact.
- local-alpha (96/118 interrupts) likely talks to the backend over localhost,
  where network blips are far less plausible — this cause fits server2-alpha
  better than the dominant offender.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- Timestamp-join: server2-alpha `Runner failed: fetch failed` / `Backend 502`
  lines against `started` → interrupt pairs on server2-alpha tasks (`db24c124`,
  `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`) — a mid-assignment crash
  proves this cause per case.
- Backend availability log (or reverse-proxy log — the 502 implies a proxy or
  gateway in front) for 11-19 → 11-21 to enumerate real downtime windows.
- Renewal/heartbeat failure semantics: confirm from code + logs that mid-run
  heartbeat loss is tolerated (lease TTL) while in-`try` call failures are
  fatal — the boundary determines how often this cause bites.

### Cause 5 — Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks, git faults)

**Summary.** A stage-end `commitAndPush` failure on the 0.1.0 build takes the
generic interrupt+rethrow path: bare interrupt, `exit(1)`, systemd restart,
re-claim, re-run, same failure — the classic crash loop. Deterministic faults
(pre-commit hook rejecting files, e.g. corrupt PNGs) loop forever until the
death bound parks the task. This is the documented "10,000 restarts" incident
class.

**Pros (for).**
- Documented precedent: task `1cae113f` survey (Round 1, Q2) states "the runner
  restarted over 10,000 times in a crash loop after the commit failed", with
  corrupt images vs the pre-commit hook as the trigger (Q6); the fix
  (deterministic-failure → failed completion, no crash; `046a6391`) merged
  11-21 09:38 — after every observed interruption — and still needs runner
  rollout.
- Code path exists and is fatal on the deployed build (generic catch at
  `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`; the 0.1.0 build predates the
  `isDeterministicGitFailure` branch).
- Comment trail in code already links rethrow-on-git-fault to "crash-loops
  under Restart=always" (`runner/daemon.js:2322-2324`) and restart storms to
  task death loops (`runner/daemon.js:2301-2303`, ref `e79b1d25`).
- `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks") shows
  hook/commit friction is a live, recurring theme, not a one-off.

**Cons (against).**
- On the forensically examined case (`7f6220c3` Merge resolver), commit+push
  SUCCEEDED in all five cycles (journal `Committed … (pushed: true)` + origin
  has the SHAs) — this cause is affirmatively ruled out there; the killer was
  the 413 (Cause 2).
- No other `finished` → interrupt case has yet been shown to lack a
  stage-output commit; worktree forensics (`kb-<taskId>` dirs, still present
  for `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`) can confirm/deny per case
  but has not been run beyond `7f6220c3`.
- Sub-15s interrupts cannot be commit failures (commit happens minutes in, post
  `finished`).

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `1cae113f` (incident record + fix), `db49d6c6` (recovery-commit hook
  failures), `e79b1d25` (referenced death-loop task) — prior art and fix
  status.
- For each remaining post-`finished` bare interrupt: does `kb-<taskId>`
  contain a stage-output commit for that execution (→ Cause 2/4 territory) or
  not (→ this cause)? Plus the daemon journal `Runner failed:` line.
- Post-rollout check: deterministic commit failures should surface as FAILED
  completions with `gitFailure` payloads (per `1cae113f`), never as interrupts.

### Cause 6 — Backend server restarts (incl. self-deploys) orphaning running tasks

**Summary.** The reporter's alternate hypothesis, and what the UI label
("Auto-resumed after server restart") literally claims: backend restarts
(`deploy.sh` `restart_service`, crashes, OOM, operator restarts) orphan
`running_*` tasks, which reconcile to `interrupted` at boot.

**Pros (for).**
- Mechanically real: `deploy.sh` full deploys call `restart_service`
  (`systemctl --user restart kainbain.service`); the reconcile path exists and
  is tested (`api/flow/scheduler/reconcileInterruptedRuns.js`).
- A real backend restart/downtime window was observed 11-20 20:40:14–20:40:57
  (build 637 `deployedAt`, engine `updatedAt`, runner-visible 502s).
- The UI labels every auto-resume "after server restart", priming this reading.

### Cause 4 — Backend-unreachable / 502 windows crashing the daemon mid-run

**Summary.** The runner daemon treats backend call failures as fatal: `fetch
failed` (undici network error) and `Backend 502` crash the process (`exit(1)` →
systemd restart). When the failure lands inside an assignment (claim, logs,
progress, complete, heartbeat/renewal handling), the generic catch reports an
interrupt (bare on 0.1.0) and the restart cycle begins. server2-alpha is a
remote runner over LAN, so it is exposed to every network blip and every
backend restart/502 window.

**Pros (for).**
- server2-alpha journal since 11-19: 501 × `fetch failed` and 16 × `Backend
  502` (`/runners/heartbeat`, `/runners/dispatch`); the idle-loop sample
  (11-19 11:15:20–11:15:44) shows three consecutive `fetch failed` crashes with
  restart counters 366→367 — proving the daemon exits rather than retries.
- A proven backend 502 window on 11-20 20:40:20–20:40:57 (seven heartbeat 502s,
  new pid each ~6s) coincides with backend build 637 `deployedAt`
  2026-11-20T20:40:14Z and `engine.updatedAt` 20:40:57Z — i.e. a real backend
  restart/downtime window, observed from the runner side.
- Any in-flight assignment spanning such a window (or a LAN blip) on the 0.1.0
  build becomes a bare interrupt — consistent with scattered bare interrupts on
  both runners.

**Cons (against).**
- The 11-20 20:40 backend restart demonstrably did NOT interrupt the in-flight
  Quick-review stage on `7f6220c3` (it completed 20:44:48), so heartbeat/502
  windows are survivable mid-run at least sometimes — the fatality depends on
  which call fails (fatal inside `executeAssignment`'s try, tolerated in the
  renewal/heartbeat path).
- No bare interrupt has yet been timestamp-matched to a specific 502/fetch-fail
  crash mid-assignment; the 501 `fetch failed` lines are dominated by idle-loop
  polls with no task impact.
- local-alpha (96/118 interrupts) likely talks to the backend over localhost,
  where network blips are far less plausible — this cause fits server2-alpha
  better than the dominant offender.

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- Timestamp-join: server2-alpha `Runner failed: fetch failed` / `Backend 502`
  lines against `started` → interrupt pairs on server2-alpha tasks (`db24c124`,
  `1f8959ca`, `f56e9878`, `ef21e99b`, `bae668cb`) — a mid-assignment crash
  proves this cause per case.

  gateway in front) for 11-19 → 11-21 to enumerate real downtime windows.
- Renewal/heartbeat failure semantics: confirm from code + logs that mid-run
  heartbeat loss is tolerated (lease TTL) while in-`try` call failures are
  fatal — the boundary determines how often this cause bites.

### Cause 5 — Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks, git faults)

**Summary.** A stage-end `commitAndPush` failure on the 0.1.0 build takes the
generic interrupt+rethrow path: bare interrupt, `exit(1)`, systemd restart,
re-claim, re-run, same failure — the classic crash loop. Deterministic faults
(pre-commit hook rejecting files, e.g. corrupt PNGs) loop forever until the
death bound parks the task. This is the documented "10,000 restarts" incident
class.

**Pros (for).**
- Documented precedent: task `1cae113f` survey (Round 1, Q2) states "the runner
  restarted over 10,000 times in a crash loop after the commit failed", with
  corrupt images vs the pre-commit hook as the trigger (Q6); the fix
  (deterministic-failure → failed completion, no crash; `046a6391`) merged
  11-21 09:38 — after every observed interruption — and still needs runner
  rollout.
- Code path exists and is fatal on the deployed build (generic catch at
  `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`; the 0.1.0 build predates the
  `isDeterministicGitFailure` branch).
- Comment trail in code already links rethrow-on-git-fault to "crash-loops
  under Restart=always" (`runner/daemon.js:2322-2324`) and restart storms to
  task death loops (`runner/daemon.js:2301-2303`, ref `e79b1d25`).

  hook/commit friction is a live, recurring theme, not a one-off.

**Cons (against).**

  SUCCEEDED in all five cycles (journal `Committed … (pushed: true)` + origin
  has the SHAs) — this cause is affirmatively ruled out there; the killer was
  the 413 (Cause 2).

  stage-output commit; worktree forensics (`kb-<taskId>` dirs, still present
  for `158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3`) can confirm/deny per case
  but has not been run beyond `7f6220c3`.

  `finished`).

**Tasks / evidence wanted.**
- `1cae113f` (incident record + fix), `db49d6c6` (recovery-commit hook
  failures), `e79b1d25` (referenced death-loop task) — prior art and fix
  status.

  contain a stage-output commit for that execution (→ Cause 2/4 territory) or
  not (→ this cause)? Plus the daemon journal `Runner failed:` line.

# Runner update runbook

Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.

## Cutting a runner release (normal path)

The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.

1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).

## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)

When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:

```
git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
```

Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
version forward instead.

## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)

1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
   resolves to the prior tag.
2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
   is cut.

Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
fleet converged.

## Migrating a host to the wrapper

Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at

   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).

   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.

   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).

4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).

## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)

When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:

```
git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
```

Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
version forward instead.

## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)

1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
   resolves to the prior tag.
2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
   is cut.

Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
fleet converged.

## Migrating a host to the wrapper

Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
so the fleet version does not change).

Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:

```
# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service

# 2. Rehearse:
scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id> --dry-run

# 3. Migrate (snapshots unit + env, reloads, restarts, re-verifies):
scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id>
```

The script refuses to overwrite an existing `current` link and prints
revert commands (copy the `.bak-<timestamp>` files back, reload,
restart). New installs need no migration: both installers
(`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`) already write
wrapper-based units. Verify after: `doctor` reports `status: ok` with
`entrypoint: wrapper`, and the next heartbeat shows the same version
as before.

## Restart vs Update (Settings › Runners)

Two separate actions, never combined:

- **Restart** reboots the runner on its **current version** — no update
  check runs. It is destructive: any work running on that runner is
  stopped at once (the claim lease expires so the work re-queues, like a
  crash). The confirm window names the runner and warns about running
  work; use it when a runner looks stuck, not to change versions.
  Mechanism: the daemon writes a `restart-requested` sentinel beside the
  install root and exits 0; the wrapper consumes it and boots the SAME
  tree again. Restart therefore needs the wrapper entrypoint — a runner
  started as bare `node main.js` exits without rebooting (migrate to the
  wrapper, above).
- **Update** reinstalls the runner onto its **target version** — the
  exact pin when the runner is pinned, otherwise the newest compatible
  release — and applies only when the runner is idle (never interrupts
  work). A busy runner queues the update for the next idle point.

## Per-runner version setting

Each runner is set to **Latest** (default) or one exact release, via
the version dropdown on its Settings › Runners detail panel:

- **Latest** tracks the newest release. It auto-updates at the next
  idle point (including right after a restart, once idle), and the
  backend nudges trailing runners at most daily. A red banner appears
  whenever a newer version exists than the one running — update (or
  wait for idle) to converge it.
- **Pinned** stays on exactly that release. Pinned runners never
  auto-update (no nudges, no idle installs, no restart-time installs);
  only the manual **Update** button installs the pin, and only when the
  pin is newer than the running version — the channel never downgrades,
  so a pin older than running shows a softer warning and the Update
  button stays disabled with the reason. Pick Latest or a newer pin to
  move forward.

The dropdown lists Latest plus every fleet-known release (newest
first): each runner's running version plus the fleet recommended and
minimum knobs — offline-safe, no release catalogue fetch.

## Triage: a runner says out of date

Start on the runner host (or ask the host owner to run it) — the
doctor is read-only and never writes:

```
$KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service
```

Match the Settings › Runners badge to a cause:

- **"update available" that never clears.** The runner trails
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (Latest runners) or its pin.
  If the doctor says `entrypoint: direct`, migrate to the wrapper
  (above) — staged updates can never boot there. If the env shows
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_AUTO_UPDATE=0` (or `(unset)` with a host-level
  opt-out), the runner acked the nudge with "skipped: auto-update is
  disabled" — flip that switch. If the runner is pinned, only the
  manual Update button installs (pins never auto-update); a pin older
  than running refuses with "never downgrades" — pick Latest or a
  newer pin. If the recommended knob sits above every published
  release, lower it to the newest release. Otherwise the runner is
  likely just busy: it converges at the next idle check, or press
  Update now (idle-only, never interrupts work). Restart does NOT
  clear this — Restart reboots the same version.
- **"restart queued" that never clears / restart loop.** The runner
  collects `requestRestart` on every heartbeat but never reboots:
  check the journal for the `Runner restarting` line. If the line is
  there but no reboot follows, the runner is not supervised by the
  wrapper (bare `node main.js` exits instead of rebooting — migrate to
  the wrapper, above) or the install root is unwritable (look for
  `sentinel not written`). A `restart-requested` file left behind by a
  crash causes at most one extra boot on the next clean exit — the
  wrapper consumes it, never loops. Old runners that predate the
  command show a disabled Restart with "too old" guidance instead —
  update them manually.
- **"below minimum" / 409 loop.** The runner is under
  `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and dispatch refuses it. It
  self-updates immediately when idle (interval bypassed). If it
  spins, check the journal for `Runner update` lines and treat the
  reason like an "update failed" below.
- **"update failed".** The next heartbeat carries `updateStatus`
  (`state: failed`, `reason`, `at`) — the badge tooltip shows it.
  Map the reason prefix: signature/key failure (release not signed
  by the pinned key — never hand-edit
  `PINNED_RELEASE_PUBLIC_KEY` in `runner/updates/verify.js` for a
  cut release); sha mismatch (re-download on next check); no asset
  for this platform (release is missing this host's tarball);
  incompatible with this backend (no newer release admits this
  backend's API — expected while the backend lags the release
  line); update lock held (a previous updater is still running or
  crashed mid-apply — stale locks self-heal); opted out (see
  above). Any failure keeps the old version running; fix the cause
  and the next idle check retries.
- **"rolled back" in the doctor.** Three crashed boots flipped
  `current` back to `previous`. Do not retry blindly: read the
  journal for the crash, fix forward with a patch release, and run
  the rollback drill above if the release is bad fleet-wide.

Backend-side checks: `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` and
`KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` values, the fleet matrix row
for the runner (`runnerVersion`, `updateAvailable`, `belowMinimum`,
`updateStatus`), and whether a `requestUpdate` command is pending or
was acked within the last 24h (the auto-nudge cooldown).
