===lib.sh===
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# lib.sh — shared helpers for the S5 ops scripts in this folder (bin/).
# Sourced, never executed directly. Shared because every script here needs
# the same three things: loud logging, loud death, and a validated HTTP GET.
#
# Rule for this task folder: an ops evidence script must never silently
# degrade. Every helper below either succeeds completely or reports a clear
# error and returns non-zero, so a baseline built from these scripts is
# trustworthy.

# log <message...> — timestamped progress line on stderr. stdout stays clean
# because the scripts print evidence tables (jsonl/tsv) on stdout.
log() {
  printf '[%s] %s\n' "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" "$*" >&2
}

# die <message...> — report a clear, fatal setup/usage error and exit 1.
# Used where there is nothing to salvage (missing tool, unreachable API,
# bad arguments). Runtime per-item failures are handled by the callers
# (recorded, counted, non-zero exit at the end) — see fleet-recount.sh.
die() {
  log "FATAL: $*"
  exit 1
}

# require_commands <cmd...> — fail before touching anything if a tool is
# missing, so the failure is about the environment, not about half-written
# evidence files.
require_commands() {
  local missing=() cmd
  for cmd in "$@"; do
    command -v "$cmd" >/dev/null 2>&1 || missing+=("$cmd")
  done
  if [ "${#missing[@]}" -gt 0 ]; then
    die "missing required commands: ${missing[*]} — install them or run on the runner host"
  fi
}

# write_atomic <dest> <src-file> — copy src-file next to dest and rename over
# it, so a crashed run never leaves a half-written evidence file that looks
# complete. Same directory => the final mv is an atomic rename.
write_atomic() {
  local dest="$1" src="$2" tmp="$dest.tmp.$$"
  if ! cp "$src" "$tmp"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: cannot write $dest"
    return 1
  fi
  mv "$tmp" "$dest"
}

# api_get_json <url> <dest> — GET url into dest as validated JSON.
#   - retries transient network failures (curl --retry-connrefused)
#   - fails on any HTTP error status (curl -f, so a 500/404 body is NOT kept)
#   - refuses to store a 200 body that is not valid JSON (an HTML error page
#     must never end up in the evidence store)
#   - writes dest atomically
# Returns non-zero with a clear stderr line on any failure.
api_get_json() {
  local url="$1" dest="$2" tmp
  tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if ! curl -sfS -m 60 --retry 3 --retry-connrefused --retry-delay 2 -o "$tmp" "$url"; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: GET $url failed (HTTP error or host unreachable after retries)"
    return 1
  fi
  if ! jq -e 'type == "object" or type == "array"' "$tmp" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    rm -f "$tmp"
    log "ERROR: GET $url returned a body that is not valid JSON — refusing to store it in $dest"
    return 1
  fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# fleet-recount.sh <label> [task-dir] — GUIDE-07 §5 fleet recount +
# WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table, over one project, read-only against the
# backend API (approved: this task's SURVEY.md q2). Scope is pinned to project
# 0fd41821-... so results compare directly with the 2026-11-21 baseline.
#
# Outputs (under task-dir, default: current directory):
#   raw/<label>/<taskId>.json        raw GET /tasks/<id> payloads (evidence)
#   recount-<label>.jsonl            one aggregated row per task  (jq/per-task.jq)
#   recount-<label>-table.json       WIDE_NET §2 aggregate         (jq/aggregate.jq)
#   recount-<label>-e5worklist.json  post-finished interrupts      (jq/e5-worklist.jq, GUIDE-05 §4 scope)
#   recount-<label>-errors.jsonl     tasks that failed to fetch/parse (only written on failure)
#   recount-<label>-meta.json        run metadata (api, project, window, counts)
#   stdout                           the §2 table + E5 worklist, for the run log
#
# Failure behaviour (deliberate, so a partial run is loud, never silent):
#   - the task list itself unreachable/invalid/empty -> exit 1, no outputs written
#   - one task fails to download or parse -> recorded in -errors.jsonl, the
#     loop continues, the table is still written, and the script exits 2 at
#     the end so the gap cannot be missed
#   - API base / project overridable via KAINBAIN_API_BASE / KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID
#     (the test suite drives this script against a local mock API)
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

main() {
  require_commands curl jq date mktemp
  local label="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$label" ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir]"
  local task_dir="${2:-$(pwd)}"
  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
  local project_id="${KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID:-0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a}"
  local raw_dir="$task_dir/raw/$label"
  mkdir -p "$raw_dir"
  local started; started="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  log "fleet-recount label=$label api=$api_base project=$project_id task_dir=$task_dir started=$started"

  # 1. task list — must be a non-empty array of well-formed ids, otherwise the
  #    API is down, the project id is wrong, or we got an error page.
  local list_tmp; list_tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if ! api_get_json "$api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id" "$list_tmp.list"; then
    rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
    die "cannot list tasks at $api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id — API down or wrong project; nothing written"
  fi
  local ids; ids="$(jq -r 'if type == "array" then (.[].id // empty) else empty end' "$list_tmp.list")"
  rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
  local n; n="$(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -c . || true)"
  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || die "GET /tasks returned zero tasks for project $project_id — refusing to write an empty baseline"
  if printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -qvE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
    die "task list contains a malformed id — refusing to continue (got: $(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' | head -3 | tr '\n' ' '))"
  fi
  log "task list ok: $n tasks"

  # 2. per-task fetch + aggregate row. One bad task never aborts the loop.
  local jsonl="$task_dir/recount-$label.jsonl" errors="$task_dir/recount-$label-errors.jsonl"
  local table="$task_dir/recount-$label-table.json" worklist="$task_dir/recount-$label-e5worklist.json"
  : > "$jsonl"
  : > "$errors"
  local ok=0 failed=0 t raw row_tmp
  row_tmp="$(mktemp)"
  for t in $ids; do
    raw="$raw_dir/$t.json"
    if api_get_json "$api_base/tasks/$t?projectId=$project_id" "$raw" \
       && jq -e 'type == "object" and ((.history // []) | type == "array")' "$raw" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && jq -c -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/per-task.jq" "$raw" > "$row_tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
      cat "$row_tmp" >> "$jsonl"
      ok=$((ok + 1))
    else
      failed=$((failed + 1))
      rm -f "$raw"
      printf '{"task":"%s","error":"fetch or parse failed"}\n' "$t" >> "$errors"
      log "WARN: task $t failed to fetch/parse — recorded in recount-$label-errors.jsonl, continuing"
    fi
  done
  rm -f "$row_tmp"
  log "fetched $ok tasks, $failed failed"

  # 3. aggregates (atomic writes), printed to stdout for the run log too.
  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/aggregate.jq" "$jsonl" > "$table.tmp" && mv "$table.tmp" "$table"
  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/e5-worklist.jq" "$jsonl" > "$worklist.tmp" && mv "$worklist.tmp" "$worklist"
  jq -n --arg label "$label" --arg api "$api_base" --arg project "$project_id" \
      --arg started "$started" --arg finished "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" \
      --argjson ok "$ok" --argjson failed "$failed" \
      '{label: $label, api: $api, project: $project, startedAt: $started, finishedAt: $finished, tasksFetched: $ok, tasksFailed: $failed}' \
    > "$task_dir/recount-$label-meta.json"

  echo "## WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table — label=$label, project $project_id, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  jq . "$table"
  echo
  echo "## E5 worklist — post-finished interrupts (GUIDE-05 §4 scope), label=$label"
  jq . "$worklist"
  echo
  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "## ERRORS — $failed task(s) failed, see recount-$label-errors.jsonl" >&2
    cat "$errors" >&2
    log "exiting 2: $failed of $n tasks failed"
    exit 2
  fi
  log "done: label=$label ok=$ok failed=$failed"
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
  main "$@"
fi

  require_commands curl jq date mktemp
  local label="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$label" ] || die "usage: fleet-recount.sh <before|after|...> [task-dir]"
  local task_dir="${2:-$(pwd)}"
  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
  local project_id="${KAINBAIN_PROJECT_ID:-0fd41821-d8a5-4e49-bc2e-28ce8c739a0a}"
  local raw_dir="$task_dir/raw/$label"
  mkdir -p "$raw_dir"
  local started; started="$(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  log "fleet-recount label=$label api=$api_base project=$project_id task_dir=$task_dir started=$started"

  # 1. task list — must be a non-empty array of well-formed ids, otherwise the
  #    API is down, the project id is wrong, or we got an error page.
  local list_tmp; list_tmp="$(mktemp)"
  if ! api_get_json "$api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id" "$list_tmp.list"; then
    rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
    die "cannot list tasks at $api_base/tasks?projectId=$project_id — API down or wrong project; nothing written"
  fi
  local ids; ids="$(jq -r 'if type == "array" then (.[].id // empty) else empty end' "$list_tmp.list")"
  rm -f "$list_tmp" "$list_tmp.list"
  local n; n="$(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -c . || true)"
  [ "$n" -gt 0 ] || die "GET /tasks returned zero tasks for project $project_id — refusing to write an empty baseline"
  if printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -qvE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$'; then
    die "task list contains a malformed id — refusing to continue (got: $(printf '%s\n' "$ids" | grep -vE '^[0-9a-f]{8}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{4}-[0-9a-f]{12}$' | head -3 | tr '\n' ' '))"
  fi
  log "task list ok: $n tasks"

  # 2. per-task fetch + aggregate row. One bad task never aborts the loop.
  local jsonl="$task_dir/recount-$label.jsonl" errors="$task_dir/recount-$label-errors.jsonl"
  local table="$task_dir/recount-$label-table.json" worklist="$task_dir/recount-$label-e5worklist.json"
  : > "$jsonl"
  : > "$errors"
  local ok=0 failed=0 t raw row_tmp
  row_tmp="$(mktemp)"
  for t in $ids; do
    raw="$raw_dir/$t.json"
    if api_get_json "$api_base/tasks/$t?projectId=$project_id" "$raw" \
       && jq -e 'type == "object" and ((.history // []) | type == "array")' "$raw" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
       && jq -c -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/per-task.jq" "$raw" > "$row_tmp" 2>/dev/null; then
      cat "$row_tmp" >> "$jsonl"
      ok=$((ok + 1))
    else
      failed=$((failed + 1))
      rm -f "$raw"
      printf '{"task":"%s","error":"fetch or parse failed"}\n' "$t" >> "$errors"
      log "WARN: task $t failed to fetch/parse — recorded in recount-$label-errors.jsonl, continuing"
    fi
  done
  rm -f "$row_tmp"
  log "fetched $ok tasks, $failed failed"

  # 3. aggregates (atomic writes), printed to stdout for the run log too.
  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/aggregate.jq" "$jsonl" > "$table.tmp" && mv "$table.tmp" "$table"
  jq -s -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/e5-worklist.jq" "$jsonl" > "$worklist.tmp" && mv "$worklist.tmp" "$worklist"
  jq -n --arg label "$label" --arg api "$api_base" --arg project "$project_id" \
      --arg started "$started" --arg finished "$(date -u +%FT%TZ)" \
      --argjson ok "$ok" --argjson failed "$failed" \
      '{label: $label, api: $api, project: $project, startedAt: $started, finishedAt: $finished, tasksFetched: $ok, tasksFailed: $failed}' \
    > "$task_dir/recount-$label-meta.json"

  echo "## WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table — label=$label, project $project_id, $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  jq . "$table"
  echo
  echo "## E5 worklist — post-finished interrupts (GUIDE-05 §4 scope), label=$label"
  jq . "$worklist"
  echo
  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "## ERRORS — $failed task(s) failed, see recount-$label-errors.jsonl" >&2
    cat "$errors" >&2
    log "exiting 2: $failed of $n tasks failed"
    exit 2
  fi
  log "done: label=$label ok=$ok failed=$failed"
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
  main "$@"
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged] — record the fleet matrix
# (GET /runners + GET /deploy/status) and a per-runner convergence verdict.
# READ-ONLY against the backend; safe to run any time, any number of times.
#
# Outputs in <outdir>:
#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not
#
# Convergence rule (S5 success criterion 1): runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the
# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
#
# Knobs (env):
#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"
#   KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT       default 046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4 (the 046a6391 deterministic-git-failure change)
#
# Exit codes: 0 snapshot written (converged or not — read verdict-<stamp>.txt);
#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# fix_in_build <buildSha|""|null> — prints true/false/null. null = cannot tell
# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
fix_in_build() {
  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo true
  else
    echo false
  fi
}

# verdict_for <runners.json> <runnerId> — prints the verdict JSON object for one
# runner (jq/runner-verdict.jq + the git ancestry check).
verdict_for() {
  local runners_json="$1" runner_id="$2" repo_root="$3" fix_commit="$4"
  local runner sha fix
  runner="$(jq -c --arg id "$runner_id" '.[] | select(.runnerId == $id) // empty' "$runners_json")"
  if [ -z "$runner" ]; then
    printf '{"runnerId":"%s","converged":false,"reasons":["runner not present in GET /runners (offline/revoked?)"]}\n' "$runner_id"
    return 0
  fi
  sha="$(printf '%s' "$runner" | jq -r '.facts.versions.build.sha // ""')"
  fix="$(fix_in_build "$sha" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
  jq -n -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runner-verdict.jq" --argjson runner "$runner" --argjson fixInBuild "$fix"
}

main() {
  require_commands curl jq git date mktemp
  local outdir="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$outdir" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged]"
  local require_converged=0
  if [ "${2:-}" = "--require-converged" ]; then require_converged=1; fi

  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
  local named="${KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS:-local-alpha,server2-alpha}"
  local fix_commit="${KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT:-046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4}"
  local task_dir repo_root stamp
  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
  mkdir -p "$outdir"

  log "runners-snapshot api=$api_base outdir=$outdir named=$named fix=$fix_commit"

  local runners_json="$outdir/runners-$stamp.json" deploy_json="$outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json"
  api_get_json "$api_base/runners" "$runners_json" \
    || die "GET $api_base/runners failed — nothing written to $outdir"
  api_get_json "$api_base/deploy/status" "$deploy_json" \
    || { log "WARN: GET /deploy/status failed — continuing with /runners only"; rm -f "$deploy_json"; }

  jq -r -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runners-tsv.jq" "$runners_json" > "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"

  local verdict_json="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.json" verdict_txt="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.txt"
  : > "$verdict_json.tmp"
  local IFS=',' r all_converged=1 v
  for r in $named; do
    v="$(verdict_for "$runners_json" "$r" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
    printf '%s\n' "$v" >> "$verdict_json.tmp"
    if printf '%s' "$v" | jq -e '.converged == true' >/dev/null; then
      printf 'CONVERGED    %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '[.runnerId, .runnerVersion, (.buildSha // "no-sha")] | join(" ")')" >> "$verdict_txt"
    else
      all_converged=0
      printf 'NOT-CONVERGED %s — %s\n' "$r" "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '.reasons | join("; ")')" >> "$verdict_txt"
    fi
  done
  jq -s '.' "$verdict_json.tmp" > "$verdict_json" && rm -f "$verdict_json.tmp"

  {
    echo "# runner convergence verdict — $(date -u +%FT%TZ) — fix commit $fix_commit"
    echo "# converged = runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND running build sha contains the fix commit"
    cat "$verdict_txt"
  } > "$verdict_txt.hdr" && mv "$verdict_txt.hdr" "$verdict_txt"

  echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} ${deploy_json:+deploy-status-$stamp.json} verdict-$stamp.{json,txt}"
  cat "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"

# Outputs in <outdir>:
#   runners-<stamp>.json        raw GET /runners payload (evidence)
#   runners-<stamp>.tsv         flat fleet table incl. build sha/builtAt
#   deploy-status-<stamp>.json  raw GET /deploy/status payload
#   verdict-<stamp>.txt         one line per named runner: CONVERGED or the reasons why not
#
# Convergence rule (S5 success criterion 1): runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the
# running build's reported git sha contains the fix commit — verified locally
# with `git merge-base --is-ancestor <fixCommit> <buildSha>`, because a version
# string alone cannot prove which code is running. If the runner reports no
# build sha, the verdict says so instead of guessing.
#
# Knobs (env):
#   KAINBAIN_API_BASE            default http://192.168.1.206:3100
#   KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS    default "local-alpha,server2-alpha"
#   KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT       default 046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4 (the 046a6391 deterministic-git-failure change)
#
# Exit codes: 0 snapshot written (converged or not — read verdict-<stamp>.txt);
#   1 setup or API failure (nothing trustworthy written);
#   3 snapshot written, --require-converged given, but not all named runners converged.
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# fix_in_build <buildSha|""|null> — prints true/false/null. null = cannot tell
# (no sha reported, or sha unknown to the local repo). Uses the local Kainbain
# checkout as the commit database — read-only git queries only.
fix_in_build() {
  local sha="$1" repo_root="$2" fix_commit="$3"
  if [ -z "$sha" ] || [ "$sha" = "null" ]; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if ! git -C "$repo_root" cat-file -e "$sha^{commit}" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo null
    return 0
  fi
  if git -C "$repo_root" merge-base --is-ancestor "$fix_commit" "$sha" 2>/dev/null; then
    echo true
  else
    echo false
  fi
}

# verdict_for <runners.json> <runnerId> — prints the verdict JSON object for one
# runner (jq/runner-verdict.jq + the git ancestry check).
verdict_for() {
  local runners_json="$1" runner_id="$2" repo_root="$3" fix_commit="$4"
  local runner sha fix
  runner="$(jq -c --arg id "$runner_id" '.[] | select(.runnerId == $id) // empty' "$runners_json")"
  if [ -z "$runner" ]; then
    printf '{"runnerId":"%s","converged":false,"reasons":["runner not present in GET /runners (offline/revoked?)"]}\n' "$runner_id"
    return 0
  fi
  sha="$(printf '%s' "$runner" | jq -r '.facts.versions.build.sha // ""')"
  fix="$(fix_in_build "$sha" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
  jq -n -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runner-verdict.jq" --argjson runner "$runner" --argjson fixInBuild "$fix"
}

main() {
  require_commands curl jq git date mktemp
  local outdir="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$outdir" ] || die "usage: runners-snapshot.sh <outdir> [--require-converged]"
  local require_converged=0
  if [ "${2:-}" = "--require-converged" ]; then require_converged=1; fi

  local api_base="${KAINBAIN_API_BASE:-http://192.168.1.206:3100}"
  local named="${KAINBAIN_S5_NAMED_RUNNERS:-local-alpha,server2-alpha}"
  local fix_commit="${KAINBAIN_S5_FIX_COMMIT:-046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4}"
  local task_dir repo_root stamp
  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  stamp="$(date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%SZ)"
  mkdir -p "$outdir"

  log "runners-snapshot api=$api_base outdir=$outdir named=$named fix=$fix_commit"

  local runners_json="$outdir/runners-$stamp.json" deploy_json="$outdir/deploy-status-$stamp.json"
  api_get_json "$api_base/runners" "$runners_json" \
    || die "GET $api_base/runners failed — nothing written to $outdir"
  api_get_json "$api_base/deploy/status" "$deploy_json" \
    || { log "WARN: GET /deploy/status failed — continuing with /runners only"; rm -f "$deploy_json"; }

  jq -r -f "$SCRIPT_DIR/jq/runners-tsv.jq" "$runners_json" > "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"

  local verdict_json="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.json" verdict_txt="$outdir/verdict-$stamp.txt"
  : > "$verdict_json.tmp"
  local IFS=',' r all_converged=1 v
  for r in $named; do
    v="$(verdict_for "$runners_json" "$r" "$repo_root" "$fix_commit")"
    printf '%s\n' "$v" >> "$verdict_json.tmp"
    if printf '%s' "$v" | jq -e '.converged == true' >/dev/null; then
      printf 'CONVERGED    %s\n' "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '[.runnerId, .runnerVersion, (.buildSha // "no-sha")] | join(" ")')" >> "$verdict_txt"
    else
      all_converged=0
      printf 'NOT-CONVERGED %s — %s\n' "$r" "$(printf '%s' "$v" | jq -r '.reasons | join("; ")')" >> "$verdict_txt"
    fi
  done
  jq -s '.' "$verdict_json.tmp" > "$verdict_json" && rm -f "$verdict_json.tmp"

  {
    echo "# runner convergence verdict — $(date -u +%FT%TZ) — fix commit $fix_commit"
    echo "# converged = runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND running build sha contains the fix commit"
    cat "$verdict_txt"
  } > "$verdict_txt.hdr" && mv "$verdict_txt.hdr" "$verdict_txt"

  echo "wrote $outdir/runners-$stamp.{json,tsv} ${deploy_json:+deploy-status-$stamp.json} verdict-$stamp.{json,txt}"
  cat "$outdir/runners-$stamp.tsv"
  echo "--- verdict:"
  cat "$verdict_txt"

  if [ "$require_converged" = 1 ] && [ "$all_converged" = 0 ]; then
    log "--require-converged: not all named runners converged (see $verdict_txt)"
    exit 3
  fi
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
  main "$@"
fi
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# server2-ssh.sh <remote command...> — run a command on the server2-alpha host
# (server2@192.168.1.172) using the password file ~/.passwrd WITHOUT ever
# printing, logging, or putting it on a command line (server2-ssh skill rules).
#
# Method: sshpass -f when installed (reads the file directly); otherwise a
# pexpect driver that opens the file inside Python and answers the prompt.
#
# Failure behaviour (this matters: a failed remote probe must not look like a
# success to the caller):
#   - no command given            -> usage on stderr, exit 64
#   - password file missing/empty  -> FATAL on stderr, exit 66 (contents never shown)
#   - password file not mode 600   -> warning on stderr (contents never shown)
#   - connect/auth timeout         -> FATAL on stderr, partial output kept, exit 124
#   - otherwise the REMOTE exit code is propagated (ssh does this natively;
#     the pexpect path reads child.exitstatus/signalstatus)
#
# Read-only usage only in this task (S5 observe-only, survey q9: never
# restart/update/reap anything on the runner hosts from here).
set -euo pipefail

PASSWORD_FILE="$HOME/.passwrd"
SSH_TARGET="server2@192.168.1.172"
SSH_OPTS=(-o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ConnectTimeout=15)

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
  echo "usage: server2-ssh.sh '<remote command>'" >&2
  exit 64
fi
if [ ! -f "$PASSWORD_FILE" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: password file $PASSWORD_FILE not found (expected mode 600, first line = password)" >&2
  exit 66
fi
MODE="$(stat -c %a "$PASSWORD_FILE")"
if [ "$MODE" != "600" ]; then
  echo "WARN: $PASSWORD_FILE has mode $MODE, expected 600 — tighten it with: chmod 600 $PASSWORD_FILE" >&2
fi

if command -v sshpass >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # sshpass consumes the file itself; the password never enters argv or env.
  exec sshpass -f "$PASSWORD_FILE" ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$SSH_TARGET" "$@"
fi

python3 - "$@" <<'PY'
import pathlib
import sys

import pexpect

password_file = pathlib.Path.home() / ".passwrd"
try:
    password = [REDACTED]().splitlines()[0].strip()
except OSError as exc:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot read {password_file}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(66)
if not password:
    print(f"FATAL: {password_file} is empty", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(66)

remote_cmd = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]) or "echo ok"
child = pexpect.spawn(
    "ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ConnectTimeout=15 server2@192.168.1.172 "
    + repr(remote_cmd),
    encoding="utf-8",
    timeout=120,
)
# No logfile is set: nothing pexpect sees (including the prompt exchange) is
# ever written anywhere.
index = child.expect(["[Pp]assword:", pexpect.EOF, pexpect.TIMEOUT])
if index == 0:
    child.sendline(password)
    index = child.expect([pexpect.EOF, pexpect.TIMEOUT])
if index == 2:  # timed out (either before or after the password prompt)
    print(child.before or "", end="")
    print("FATAL: ssh to server2@192.168.1.172 timed out", file=sys.stderr)
    child.close(force=True)
    sys.exit(124)

for line in (child.before or "").splitlines():
    if "Warning: Permanently added" in line:
        continue
    print(line)

child.close(force=True)
if child.exitstatus is not None:
    sys.exit(child.exitstatus)
if child.signalstatus is not None:
    sys.exit(128 + child.signalstatus)
sys.exit(1)
PY

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>... — GUIDE-05 §4 E5 forensics
# sweep. READ-ONLY: it never reaps, deletes, restarts, updates, or modifies
# anything on either host (survey q9: observe only). For each kb-<taskId>
# it records, per host:
#   - worktrees under the work root: existence + git log + whether a
#     stage-output commit is present in HEAD history
#   - origin branch refs (refs/remotes/origin/kb/<id>* and kb-<id>*): the
#     durable evidence that survives worktree reaping, with git log
#   - journal lines for the task id (Runner failed / commit / hook / 413 /
#     502 / fetch failed / interrupt)
# and prints one VERDICT line per task:
#   stage-output commit PRESENT  -> Cause 2/4 territory (GUIDE-05 §4)
#   evidence found, commit ABSENT -> Cause 5 suspect (commit/push loop with no landed output)
#   no worktree and no origin ref -> evidence gap (reaped/branch deleted)
#
# Safety: task-id arguments are validated (hex/dashes only — injection guard,
# see lib.sh) and the remote probe is sent base64-encoded, so no argument can
# break out of the remote shell. The probe itself runs only ls/git
# log/for-each-ref/journalctl — all read-only.
#
# Usage:
#   bin/e5-sweep.sh local   7f6220c3 db49d6c6 ...
#   bin/e5-sweep.sh server2 158394ab ...
# Env overrides (used by the test suite, harmless in prod):
#   E5_WORK_ROOT  E5_UNIT  E5_ORIGIN_REPO  E5_JOURNAL_SINCE
# Exit codes: 0 all probed; 1 usage/setup error; 2 some probes failed (output
# still written — the summary says which).
set -euo pipefail
SCRIPT_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
# shellcheck source=lib.sh
source "$SCRIPT_DIR/lib.sh"

# The probe body. Fixed text — the only variables are its five positional
# arguments, all validated or script-controlled before this runs anywhere.
PROBE_SCRIPT='
set -uo pipefail
WORK_ROOT="$1"; UNIT="$2"; ORIGIN_REPO="$3"; PREFIX="$4"; SINCE="$5"
stage_present=0; any_evidence=0

echo "== task kb-$PREFIX"
echo "-- worktrees under $WORK_ROOT:"
found=0
for d in "$WORK_ROOT"/kb-"$PREFIX"*; do
  [ -d "$d" ] || continue
  found=1; any_evidence=1
  echo "   worktree: $d (branch: $(git -C "$d" branch --show-current 2>/dev/null || echo "?"))"
  git -C "$d" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -5 2>&1 | head -6 || true
  if git -C "$d" log --format=%s -20 2>/dev/null | grep -qi "stage output"; then
    stage_present=1
    echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT in worktree HEAD history"
  else
    echo "     stage-output-commit: absent in worktree HEAD history"
  fi
  for ref in $(git -C "$d" for-each-ref --format="%(refname)" "refs/remotes/origin/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/remotes/origin/kb-$PREFIX"* 2>/dev/null); do
    echo "   origin ref: $ref"
    git -C "$d" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -5 "$ref" 2>&1 | head -6 || true
    if git -C "$d" log --format=%s -20 "$ref" 2>/dev/null | grep -qi "stage output"; then
      stage_present=1
      echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT on $ref"
    else
      echo "     stage-output-commit: absent on $ref"
    fi
  done
done
[ "$found" = 1 ] || echo "   (no worktree on this host)"

echo "-- origin branch refs in $ORIGIN_REPO (durable, survives worktree reaping):"
if git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" rev-parse --git-dir >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  refs=$(git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" for-each-ref --format="%(refname)" "refs/remotes/origin/kb/$PREFIX"* "refs/remotes/origin/kb-$PREFIX"* 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$refs" ]; then
    any_evidence=1
    while IFS= read -r ref; do
      echo "   $ref"
      git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" log --format="     %h %ci %s" -8 "$ref" 2>&1 | head -9 || true
      if git -C "$ORIGIN_REPO" log --format=%s -20 "$ref" 2>/dev/null | grep -qi "stage output"; then
        stage_present=1
        echo "     stage-output-commit: PRESENT on $ref"
      else
        echo "     stage-output-commit: absent on $ref"
      fi
    done <<EOF
$refs
EOF
  else
    echo "   (no origin branch kb/$PREFIX* or kb-$PREFIX*)"
  fi
else
  echo "   (origin repo $ORIGIN_REPO not available on this host — evidence gap note)"
fi

echo "-- journal ($UNIT, since $SINCE) lines matching $PREFIX:"
if command -v journalctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  journalctl --user -u "$UNIT" --since "$SINCE" --no-pager 2>/dev/null \
    | grep -i -- "$PREFIX" | grep -iE "Runner failed|commit|hook|413|502|fetch failed|interrupt" | tail -15 | sed "s/^/   /" \
    || echo "   (no matching journal lines)"
else
  echo "   (journalctl not available on this host)"
fi

if [ "$stage_present" = 1 ]; then
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: stage-output commit PRESENT -> Cause 2/4 territory (GUIDE-05 §4)"
elif [ "$any_evidence" = 1 ]; then
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: evidence found but no stage-output commit -> Cause 5 suspect (commit/push loop, no landed output)"
else
  echo "VERDICT kb-$PREFIX: no worktree and no origin branch -> evidence gap (worktree reaped and branch deleted)"
fi
echo
'

# run_probe <host> <work_root> <unit> <origin_repo> <prefix> <since>
# Local: pipe the probe into bash directly. server2: base64-encode the probe
# and decode it on the remote side, so argument quoting can never inject.
run_probe() {
  local host="$1"; shift
  local args; args="$(printf '%q ' "$@")"
  if [ "$host" = "server2" ]; then
    local b64
    b64="$(printf '%s' "$PROBE_SCRIPT" | base64 -w0)"
    "$SCRIPT_DIR/server2-ssh.sh" "echo $b64 | base64 -d | bash -s -- $args"
  else
    printf '%s' "$PROBE_SCRIPT" | bash -s -- "$@"
  fi
}

main() {
  require_commands bash base64 date
  local host="${1:-}"
  [ -n "$host" ] || die "usage: e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>..."
  [ "$host" = "local" ] || [ "$host" = "server2" ] || die "host must be 'local' or 'server2', got '$host'"
  shift
  [ $# -ge 1 ] || die "usage: e5-sweep.sh <local|server2> <taskId-prefix>... (at least one task id)"
  validate_task_prefix "$@"

  local task_dir repo_root work_root unit origin_repo since
  task_dir="$(cd "$SCRIPT_DIR/.." && pwd)"
  repo_root="$(git -C "$task_dir" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
  since="${E5_JOURNAL_SINCE:-2026-11-19}"
  if [ "$host" = "server2" ]; then
    work_root="${E5_WORK_ROOT:-/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work}"
    unit="${E5_UNIT:-kainbain-runner-server2-alpha}"
    origin_repo="${E5_ORIGIN_REPO:-/home/[REDACTED]/.kainbain/runner-work/mirrors/Kainbain}"
    require_commands git
  else
    work_root="${E5_WORK_ROOT:-$HOME/.kainbain/runner-work}"
    unit="${E5_UNIT:-kainbain-runner-local-alpha}"
    origin_repo="${E5_ORIGIN_REPO:-$repo_root}"
    require_commands git
  fi

  echo "## E5 sweep host=$host work_root=$work_root unit=$unit origin_repo=$origin_repo since=$since at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  local failed=0 t
  for t in "$@"; do
    if ! run_probe "$host" "$work_root" "$unit" "$origin_repo" "$t" "$since"; then
      failed=$((failed + 1))
      log "WARN: probe for kb-$t on $host failed — recorded, continuing with the next task"
      echo "VERDICT kb-$t: PROBE FAILED on $host (see stderr) — treat as evidence gap"
      echo
    fi
  done
  echo "## E5 sweep done: $# task(s), $failed probe failure(s) at $(date -u +%FT%TZ)"
  if [ "$failed" -gt 0 ]; then
    log "exiting 2: $failed probe(s) failed"
    exit 2
  fi
}

if [ "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}" = "$0" ]; then
  main "$@"
fi

# (input: `jq -s` over recount-<label>.jsonl). Pinned by bin/tests/run-tests.sh
# against recount-before-table.json.
{
  tasks_total: length,
  tasks_with_interrupts: ([.[] | select(.runner_interrupts > 0)] | length),
  runner_interrupts: ([.[].runner_interrupts] | add // 0),
  with_reason: ([.[].with_reason] | add // 0),
  bare: ([.[].bare] | add // 0),
  per_runner: ([.[].per_runner[]?] | group_by(.runner) | map({runner: .[0].runner, n: (map(.n) | add)}) | sort_by(.runner)),
  le15s_after_started: ([.[].interrupt_details[]? | select(.delta_s_from_started != null and .delta_s_from_started <= 15)] | length),
  ge120s_after_started: ([.[].interrupt_details[]? | select(.delta_s_from_started != null and .delta_s_from_started >= 120)] | length),
  post_finished_interrupts: ([.[].interrupt_details[]? | select(.prev_progress_event != null and (.prev_progress_event | test(": finished$")))] | length),
  median_delta_s: ([.[].interrupt_details[]? | select(.delta_s_from_started != null) | .delta_s_from_started] | sort as $d | (if ($d | length) > 0 then $d[($d | length) / 2] else null end)),
  auto_resumed: ([.[].auto_resumed] | add // 0),
  server_restart: ([.[].server_restart] | add // 0),
  recovered_server_restart: ([.[].recovered_server_restart] | add // 0),
  escalated: ([.[].escalated] | add // 0),
  failed_stage_actions: ([.[].failed_stage] | add // 0),
  tasks_with_git_failure_streak: ([.[] | select(.git_failure_streak > 0)] | length),
  reason_vocabulary: ([.[].reasons[]?] | unique)
}
# per-task.jq — turn one raw GET /tasks/<id> payload into one aggregated row.
# Consumed by bin/fleet-recount.sh. The output shape is pinned by
# bin/tests/run-tests.sh against the recorded before-fixtures — change it
# only together with the tests and the before/after tables.
#
# Defensive notes: every .action access goes through (// "") and runner/reason
# extraction uses match() (which yields no output on no-match) instead of
# capture() (which hard-errors), so one odd history row can never abort the
# whole recount.
def ts: if type == "string" then sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601 else null end;
def runnerOf($action): [$action | match("Runner (?<r>[^ ]+) interrupted execution") | .captures[0].string] | first // "unknown";
def reasonOf($action): if ($action | test("Reason:")) then [$action | match("Reason: (?<x>.*)$") | .captures[0].string] | first else null end;

. as $t |
# history may be missing or not an array on a malformed payload — treat as
# empty rather than aborting the whole recount.
def hist: ($t.history // []) | if type == "array" then . else [] end;
([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("interrupted execution"))]) as $ints |
{
  task: $t.id,
  status: $t.status,
  runner_interrupts: ($ints | length),
  with_reason: ([$ints[] | select((.action // "") | test("Reason:"))] | length),
  bare: ([$ints[] | select((.action // "") | test("Reason:") | not)] | length),
  per_runner: ($ints | map(runnerOf(.action)) | group_by(.) | map({runner: .[0], n: length})),
  reasons: ([$ints[] | reasonOf(.action) | select(. != null)] | unique),
  auto_resumed: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Auto-resumed after server restart"))] | length),
  server_restart: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("interrupted by server restart"))] | length),
  recovered_server_restart: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Execution recovered after server restart"))] | length),
  escalated: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Runner deaths escalated"))] | length),
  failed_stage: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Stage failed in|Failed back to stage"))] | length),
  git_failure_streak: (($t.gitFailureStreak // {}).count // 0),
  last_error_git_kind: ((($t.lastError // {}).gitDiagnostics // {}).kind // null),
  interrupt_details: [
    hist | to_entries[] | select((.value.action // "") | test("interrupted execution")) |
    .key as $i | .value |
    (hist[0:$i] | map(select((.action // "") | test(": started$"))) | last) as $s |
    (hist[0:$i] | map(select((.action // "") | test(": (started|prompted|finished)$"))) | last) as $p |
    {
      ts: .timestamp,
      runner: runnerOf(.action),
      reason: reasonOf(.action),
      delta_s_from_started: (if $s and ((.timestamp | ts) != null) and (($s.timestamp | ts) != null) then ((.timestamp | ts) - ($s.timestamp | ts)) else null end),
      prev_progress_event: ($p.action // null)
    }
  ]
}

# e5-worklist.jq — GUIDE-05 §4 scope: tasks with at least one post-`finished`
# interrupt (input: `jq -s` over recount-<label>.jsonl). Each entry keeps only
# the post-finished interrupt details.
[.[] | {
  task,
  interrupt_details: [.interrupt_details[] | select(.prev_progress_event != null and (.prev_progress_event | test(": finished$")))]
} | select(.interrupt_details | length > 0)]
# runner-verdict.jq — S5 convergence verdict for one runner.
# Input:  { "runner": <runner object from GET /runners>, "fixInBuild": <true|false|null> }
#   fixInBuild is computed by the shell with `git merge-base --is-ancestor
#   <fixCommit> <buildSha>` (null when no build sha is reported or the sha is
#   unknown to the local repo) — a version string alone proves nothing.
# Converged = runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the running build contains the fix.
def semverAtLeast($v; $min): ($v | split(".") | map(tonumber? // 0)) >= ($min | split(".") | map(tonumber? // 0));

. as $in | $in.runner as $r |
(semverAtLeast($r.runnerVersion // "0"; "0.2.0")) as $versionOk |
{
  runnerId: $r.runnerId,
  status: $r.status,
  runnerVersion: $r.runnerVersion,
  buildSha: ($r.facts.versions.build.sha // null),
  recommendedVersion: $r.recommendedVersion,
  updateAvailable: $r.updateAvailable,
  versionOk: $versionOk,
  fixInBuild: $in.fixInBuild,
  converged: ($versionOk and ($in.fixInBuild == true)),
  reasons: (
    (if $versionOk then [] else ["runnerVersion \($r.runnerVersion // "?") is below 0.2.0"] end)
    + (if $in.fixInBuild == true then []
       elif $in.fixInBuild == false then ["running build \($r.facts.versions.build.sha // "?") does not contain the deterministic-git-failure fix commit"]
       else ["no build sha reported (or unknown locally) — cannot verify the fix is in the running build"] end)
  )
}
# runners-tsv.jq — flatten GET /runners into a TSV (header row first).
# Includes the runner-reported build sha/builtAt, because the version string
# alone cannot prove the running build contains a given fix commit.
# Fails loud on non-array input instead of emitting a mangled table.
if type != "array" then error("runners-tsv.jq: expected an array of runner objects, got \(type)") else
  (
    ["runnerId", "status", "runnerVersion", "buildSha", "buildBuiltAt", "recommended", "minimum", "desired", "availableVersions", "updateAvailable", "belowMinimum", "updateStatus", "pendingCommands", "lastSeenAt"],
    (.[] | [
      .runnerId,
      .status,
      .runnerVersion,
      (.facts.versions.build.sha // ""),
      (.facts.versions.build.builtAt // ""),
      .recommendedVersion,
      .minimumVersion,
      .desiredVersion,
      ([.availableVersions[]] | join(",")),
      (.updateAvailable | tostring),
      (.belowMinimum | tostring),
      (if .updateStatus == null then "" else (.updateStatus | tostring) end),
      ([.pendingCommands[]?] | map(.command // .) | join(",")),
      (.lastSeenAt // "")
    ])
  ) | @tsv
end

# e5-worklist.jq — GUIDE-05 §4 scope: tasks with at least one post-`finished`
# interrupt (input: `jq -s` over recount-<label>.jsonl). Each entry keeps only
# the post-finished interrupt details.
[.[] | {
  task,
  interrupt_details: [.interrupt_details[] | select(.prev_progress_event != null and (.prev_progress_event | test(": finished$")))]
} | select(.interrupt_details | length > 0)]
# runner-verdict.jq — S5 convergence verdict for one runner.
# Input:  { "runner": <runner object from GET /runners>, "fixInBuild": <true|false|null> }
#   fixInBuild is computed by the shell with `git merge-base --is-ancestor
#   <fixCommit> <buildSha>` (null when no build sha is reported or the sha is
#   unknown to the local repo) — a version string alone proves nothing.
# Converged = runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the running build contains the fix.
def semverAtLeast($v; $min): ($v | split(".") | map(tonumber? // 0)) >= ($min | split(".") | map(tonumber? // 0));

. as $in | $in.runner as $r |
(semverAtLeast($r.runnerVersion // "0"; "0.2.0")) as $versionOk |
{
  runnerId: $r.runnerId,
  status: $r.status,
  runnerVersion: $r.runnerVersion,
  buildSha: ($r.facts.versions.build.sha // null),
  recommendedVersion: $r.recommendedVersion,
  updateAvailable: $r.updateAvailable,
  versionOk: $versionOk,
  fixInBuild: $in.fixInBuild,
  converged: ($versionOk and ($in.fixInBuild == true)),
  reasons: (
    (if $versionOk then [] else ["runnerVersion \($r.runnerVersion // "?") is below 0.2.0"] end)
    + (if $in.fixInBuild == true then []
       elif $in.fixInBuild == false then ["running build \($r.facts.versions.build.sha // "?") does not contain the deterministic-git-failure fix commit"]
       else ["no build sha reported (or unknown locally) — cannot verify the fix is in the running build"] end)
  )
}
# runners-tsv.jq — flatten GET /runners into a TSV (header row first).
# Includes the runner-reported build sha/builtAt, because the version string
# alone cannot prove the running build contains a given fix commit.
# Fails loud on non-array input instead of emitting a mangled table.
if type != "array" then error("runners-tsv.jq: expected an array of runner objects, got \(type)") else
  (
    ["runnerId", "status", "runnerVersion", "buildSha", "buildBuiltAt", "recommended", "minimum", "desired", "availableVersions", "updateAvailable", "belowMinimum", "updateStatus", "pendingCommands", "lastSeenAt"],
    (.[] | [
      .runnerId,
      .status,
      .runnerVersion,
      (.facts.versions.build.sha // ""),
      (.facts.versions.build.builtAt // ""),
      .recommendedVersion,
      .minimumVersion,
      .desiredVersion,
      ([.availableVersions[]] | join(",")),
      (.updateAvailable | tostring),
      (.belowMinimum | tostring),
      (if .updateStatus == null then "" else (.updateStatus | tostring) end),
      ([.pendingCommands[]?] | map(.command // .) | join(",")),
      (.lastSeenAt // "")
    ])
  ) | @tsv
end

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# run-tests.sh — offline test suite for the S5 ops scripts in bin/.
#
# Nothing here touches prod: the suite uses the recorded evidence fixtures
# (raw/before/*.json, runners-before/*.json), synthetic fixtures it builds
# itself, and a local mock API (bin/tests/mock-api.py) on 127.0.0.1.
#
# What is pinned:
#   - jq/per-task.jq + jq/aggregate.jq over all raw/before fixtures must
#     reproduce recount-before-table.json exactly (regression guard for the
#     before/after comparison)
#   - edge cases: reasoned interrupts, gitFailureStreak/lastError.gitDiagnostics,
#     post-finished interrupts, missing history, non-object payloads
#   - jq/runner-verdict.jq convergence rules + the git ancestry check
#   - the E5 probe classification (present / absent / evidence-gap / probe-failed)
#   - fleet-recount.sh end-to-end against the mock API: success, partial
#     failure (exit 2, errors file, table still written), empty list (exit 1)
#   - runners-snapshot.sh end-to-end against the mock API, incl.
#     --require-converged exit 3
#   - lib.sh api_get_json failure modes (HTTP 500, invalid JSON, connection
#     refused) and the e5-sweep task-id injection guard
#
# Run: bin/tests/run-tests.sh   (exit 0 = all pass)
set -euo pipefail
TESTS_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)"
BIN_DIR="$(cd "$TESTS_DIR/.." && pwd)"
TASK_DIR="$(cd "$BIN_DIR/.." && pwd)"
REPO_ROOT="$(git -C "$TASK_DIR" rev-parse --show-toplevel)"
FIXTURE_RAW="$TASK_DIR/raw/before"
FIXTURE_RUNNERS="$(ls "$TASK_DIR"/runners-before/runners-*.json | head -1)"
FIXTURE_DEPLOY="$(ls "$TASK_DIR"/runners-before/deploy-status-*.json | head -1)"
FIX_COMMIT="046a63917d52181d00efbd4a6624bd1c53131fa4"

pass=0 fail=0
ok()  { pass=$((pass + 1)); echo "PASS: $1"; }
bad() { fail=$((fail + 1)); echo "FAIL: $1"; }
# check_eq <name> <expected> <actual>
check_eq() {
  if [ "$2" = "$3" ]; then ok "$1"; else bad "$1 — expected [$2], got [$3]"; fi
}
# check_file_eq <name> <fileA> <fileB> — compares after canonical jq -S (JSON) or plain diff
check_json_eq() {
  if diff -q <(jq -S . "$2") <(jq -S . "$3") >/dev/null 2>&1; then ok "$1"; else bad "$1 — $2 != $3"; diff <(jq -S . "$2") <(jq -S . "$3") | head -10 || true; fi
}

WORK="$(mktemp -d)"
trap 'rm -rf "$WORK"' EXIT

# shellcheck source=../lib.sh
source "$BIN_DIR/lib.sh"

echo "== T1: per-task.jq + aggregate.jq over recorded before-fixtures reproduce the pinned table"
: > "$WORK/rows.jsonl"
for f in "$FIXTURE_RAW"/*.json; do
  jq -c -f "$BIN_DIR/jq/per-task.jq" "$f" >> "$WORK/rows.jsonl"
done
check_eq "T1 row count" "$(ls "$FIXTURE_RAW"/*.json | wc -l)" "$(wc -l < "$WORK/rows.jsonl" | tr -d ' ')"
jq -s -f "$BIN_DIR/jq/aggregate.jq" "$WORK/rows.jsonl" > "$WORK/table.json"
check_json_eq "T1 aggregate == recount-before-table.json" "$WORK/table.json" "$TASK_DIR/recount-before-table.json"

echo "== T2: per-task.jq edge cases (synthetic payloads)"
mkdir -p "$WORK/fix"
jq -n '{
  id: "aaaaaaaa-1111-2222-3333-444444444444", status: "in_stage",
  gitFailureStreak: {count: 2}, lastError: {gitDiagnostics: {kind: "hook_rejected"}},
  history: [
    {timestamp: "2026-11-22T10:00:00Z", action: "Runner local-alpha stage 1: started"},
    {timestamp: "2026-11-22T10:00:04.500Z", action: "Runner local-alpha interrupted execution e1 — lease dropped, re-queues as interrupted. Reason: Runner workdir unavailable: cap reached"},
    {timestamp: "2026-11-22T10:05:00Z", action: "Runner local-alpha stage 1: finished"},
    {timestamp: "2026-11-22T10:06:30Z", action: "Runner server2-alpha interrupted execution e2 — lease dropped, re-queues as interrupted."},
    {timestamp: "2026-11-22T10:07:00Z", action: "Runner deaths escalated to runner-death-loop"},
    {timestamp: "2026-11-22T10:07:01Z", action: "Auto-resumed after server restart"},
    {timestamp: "2026-11-22T10:07:02Z", action: "Stage failed in stage 1"}
  ]
}' > "$WORK/fix/edge1.json"
jq -n '{id: "bbbbbbbb-1111-2222-3333-444444444444", status: "done"}' > "$WORK/fix/edge2-nohistory.json"
jq -c -f "$BIN_DIR/jq/per-task.jq" "$WORK/fix/edge1.json" > "$WORK/edge1.row"
check_eq "T2 reasoned interrupt counted" "1" "$(jq -r '.with_reason' "$WORK/edge1.row")"
check_eq "T2 bare interrupt counted" "1" "$(jq -r '.bare' "$WORK/edge1.row")"
check_eq "T2 reason text" "Runner workdir unavailable: cap reached" "$(jq -r '.reasons[0]' "$WORK/edge1.row")"
check_eq "T2 git_failure_streak" "2" "$(jq -r '.git_failure_streak' "$WORK/edge1.row")"
check_eq "T2 last_error_git_kind" "hook_rejected" "$(jq -r '.last_error_git_kind' "$WORK/edge1.row")"
check_eq "T2 escalated" "1" "$(jq -r '.escalated' "$WORK/edge1.row")"
check_eq "T2 auto_resumed" "1" "$(jq -r '.auto_resumed' "$WORK/edge1.row")"
check_eq "T2 post-finished interrupt detail present" "1" "$(jq -r '[.interrupt_details[] | select(.prev_progress_event | test(": finished$"))] | length' "$WORK/edge1.row")"
# deltas are whole seconds: fromdateiso8601 truncates the fractional part
check_eq "T2 fractional-second delta computed (whole seconds)" "4" "$(jq -r '[.interrupt_details[] | select(.runner == "local-alpha")] | .[0].delta_s_from_started' "$WORK/edge1.row")"
check_eq "T2 no-fraction timestamp delta (10:06:30 - 10:00:00)" "390" "$(jq -r '[.interrupt_details[] | select(.runner == "server2-alpha")] | .[0].delta_s_from_started' "$WORK/edge1.row")"
jq -c -f "$BIN_DIR/jq/per-task.jq" "$WORK/fix/edge2-nohistory.json" > "$WORK/edge2.row"
check_eq "T2 missing history does not crash" "0" "$(jq -r '.runner_interrupts' "$WORK/edge2.row")"
if echo '"just a string"' | jq -c -f "$BIN_DIR/jq/per-task.jq" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  bad "T2 non-object payload should fail loudly"
else
  ok "T2 non-object payload fails loudly (non-zero), not silently"
fi

echo "== T3: aggregate.jq arithmetic on hand-built rows"
cat > "$WORK/agg-rows.jsonl" <<'EOF'
{"task":"t1","runner_interrupts":2,"with_reason":1,"bare":1,"per_runner":[{"runner":"local-alpha","n":2}],"interrupt_details":[{"delta_s_from_started":3,"prev_progress_event":"x: finished"},{"delta_s_from_started":200,"prev_progress_event":"y: started"}],"auto_resumed":1,"server_restart":0,"recovered_server_restart":0,"escalated":1,"failed_stage":0,"git_failure_streak":0,"reasons":["r1"],"last_error_git_kind":null}
{"task":"t2","runner_interrupts":1,"with_reason":0,"bare":1,"per_runner":[{"runner":"server2-alpha","n":1}],"interrupt_details":[{"delta_s_from_started":10,"prev_progress_event":"z: finished"}],"auto_resumed":0,"server_restart":0,"recovered_server_restart":0,"escalated":0,"failed_stage":2,"git_failure_streak":3,"reasons":[],"last_error_git_kind":"push_rejected"}
EOF
jq -s -f "$BIN_DIR/jq/aggregate.jq" "$WORK/agg-rows.jsonl" > "$WORK/agg.json"
check_eq "T3 totals" "3" "$(jq -r '.runner_interrupts' "$WORK/agg.json")"
check_eq "T3 bare" "2" "$(jq -r '.bare' "$WORK/agg.json")"
check_eq "T3 le15s" "2" "$(jq -r '.le15s_after_started' "$WORK/agg.json")"
check_eq "T3 ge120s" "1" "$(jq -r '.ge120s_after_started' "$WORK/agg.json")"
check_eq "T3 post_finished" "2" "$(jq -r '.post_finished_interrupts' "$WORK/agg.json")"
check_eq "T3 git streak tasks" "1" "$(jq -r '.tasks_with_git_failure_streak' "$WORK/agg.json")"
check_eq "T3 per_runner merge" "local-alpha:2,server2-alpha:1" "$(jq -r '.per_runner | map("\(.runner):\(.n)") | join(",")' "$WORK/agg.json")"

echo "== T4: e5-worklist.jq scope"
jq -s -f "$BIN_DIR/jq/e5-worklist.jq" "$WORK/agg-rows.jsonl" > "$WORK/e5.json"
check_eq "T4 both tasks in worklist" "2" "$(jq -r 'length' "$WORK/e5.json")"
check_eq "T4 only post-finished details kept" "1" "$(jq -r '.[0].interrupt_details | length' "$WORK/e5.json")"

echo "== T5: runners-tsv.jq over the recorded runners fixture"
jq -r -f "$BIN_DIR/jq/runners-tsv.jq" "$FIXTURE_RUNNERS" > "$WORK/runners.tsv"
check_eq "T5 header + one line per runner" "10" "$(wc -l < "$WORK/runners.tsv" | tr -d ' ')"
check_eq "T5 header first column" "runnerId" "$(head -1 "$WORK/runners.tsv" | cut -f1)"
check_eq "T5 local-alpha version column" "0.1.0" "$(awk -F'\t' '$1=="local-alpha"{print $3}' "$WORK/runners.tsv")"

# per-task.jq — turn one raw GET /tasks/<id> payload into one aggregated row.
# Consumed by bin/fleet-recount.sh. The output shape is pinned by
# bin/tests/run-tests.sh against the recorded before-fixtures — change it
# only together with the tests and the before/after tables.
#
# Defensive notes: every .action access goes through (// "") and runner/reason
# extraction uses match() (which yields no output on no-match) instead of
# capture() (which hard-errors), so one odd history row can never abort the
# whole recount.
def ts: if type == "string" then sub("\\.[0-9]+Z$"; "Z") | fromdateiso8601 else null end;
def runnerOf($action): [$action | match("Runner (?<r>[^ ]+) interrupted execution") | .captures[0].string] | first // "unknown";
def reasonOf($action): if ($action | test("Reason:")) then [$action | match("Reason: (?<x>.*)$") | .captures[0].string] | first else null end;

. as $t |
# history may be missing or not an array on a malformed payload — treat as
# empty rather than aborting the whole recount.
def hist: ($t.history // []) | if type == "array" then . else [] end;
([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("interrupted execution"))]) as $ints |
{
  task: $t.id,
  status: $t.status,
  runner_interrupts: ($ints | length),
  with_reason: ([$ints[] | select((.action // "") | test("Reason:"))] | length),
  bare: ([$ints[] | select((.action // "") | test("Reason:") | not)] | length),
  per_runner: ($ints | map(runnerOf(.action)) | group_by(.) | map({runner: .[0], n: length})),
  reasons: ([$ints[] | reasonOf(.action) | select(. != null)] | unique),
  auto_resumed: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Auto-resumed after server restart"))] | length),
  server_restart: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("interrupted by server restart"))] | length),
  recovered_server_restart: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Execution recovered after server restart"))] | length),
  escalated: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Runner deaths escalated"))] | length),
  failed_stage: ([hist[]? | select((.action // "") | test("Stage failed in|Failed back to stage"))] | length),
  git_failure_streak: (($t.gitFailureStreak // {}).count // 0),
  last_error_git_kind: ((($t.lastError // {}).gitDiagnostics // {}).kind // null),
  interrupt_details: [
    hist | to_entries[] | select((.value.action // "") | test("interrupted execution")) |
    .key as $i | .value |
    (hist[0:$i] | map(select((.action // "") | test(": started$"))) | last) as $s |
    (hist[0:$i] | map(select((.action // "") | test(": (started|prompted|finished)$"))) | last) as $p |
    {
      ts: .timestamp,
      runner: runnerOf(.action),
      reason: reasonOf(.action),
      delta_s_from_started: (if $s and ((.timestamp | ts) != null) and (($s.timestamp | ts) != null) then ((.timestamp | ts) - ($s.timestamp | ts)) else null end),
      prev_progress_event: ($p.action // null)
    }
  ]
}
# aggregate.jq — WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2 table over an array of per-task rows
# (input: `jq -s` over recount-<label>.jsonl). Pinned by bin/tests/run-tests.sh
# against recount-before-table.json.
{
  tasks_total: length,
  tasks_with_interrupts: ([.[] | select(.runner_interrupts > 0)] | length),
  runner_interrupts: ([.[].runner_interrupts] | add // 0),
  with_reason: ([.[].with_reason] | add // 0),
  bare: ([.[].bare] | add // 0),
  per_runner: ([.[].per_runner[]?] | group_by(.runner) | map({runner: .[0].runner, n: (map(.n) | add)}) | sort_by(.runner)),
  le15s_after_started: ([.[].interrupt_details[]? | select(.delta_s_from_started != null and .delta_s_from_started <= 15)] | length),
  ge120s_after_started: ([.[].interrupt_details[]? | select(.delta_s_from_started != null and .delta_s_from_started >= 120)] | length),
  post_finished_interrupts: ([.[].interrupt_details[]? | select(.prev_progress_event != null and (.prev_progress_event | test(": finished$")))] | length),
  median_delta_s: ([.[].interrupt_details[]? | select(.delta_s_from_started != null) | .delta_s_from_started] | sort as $d | (if ($d | length) > 0 then $d[($d | length) / 2] else null end)),
  auto_resumed: ([.[].auto_resumed] | add // 0),
  server_restart: ([.[].server_restart] | add // 0),
  recovered_server_restart: ([.[].recovered_server_restart] | add // 0),
  escalated: ([.[].escalated] | add // 0),
  failed_stage_actions: ([.[].failed_stage] | add // 0),
  tasks_with_git_failure_streak: ([.[] | select(.git_failure_streak > 0)] | length),
  reason_vocabulary: ([.[].reasons[]?] | unique)
}
# e5-worklist.jq — GUIDE-05 §4 scope: tasks with at least one post-`finished`
# interrupt (input: `jq -s` over recount-<label>.jsonl). Each entry keeps only
# the post-finished interrupt details.
[.[] | {
  task,
  interrupt_details: [.interrupt_details[] | select(.prev_progress_event != null and (.prev_progress_event | test(": finished$")))]
} | select(.interrupt_details | length > 0)]
# runners-tsv.jq — flatten GET /runners into a TSV (header row first).
# Includes the runner-reported build sha/builtAt, because the version string
# alone cannot prove the running build contains a given fix commit.
# Fails loud on non-array input instead of emitting a mangled table.
if type != "array" then error("runners-tsv.jq: expected an array of runner objects, got \(type)") else
  (
    ["runnerId", "status", "runnerVersion", "buildSha", "buildBuiltAt", "recommended", "minimum", "desired", "availableVersions", "updateAvailable", "belowMinimum", "updateStatus", "pendingCommands", "lastSeenAt"],
    (.[] | [
      .runnerId,
      .status,
      .runnerVersion,
      (.facts.versions.build.sha // ""),
      (.facts.versions.build.builtAt // ""),
      .recommendedVersion,
      .minimumVersion,
      .desiredVersion,
      ([.availableVersions[]] | join(",")),
      (.updateAvailable | tostring),
      (.belowMinimum | tostring),
      (if .updateStatus == null then "" else (.updateStatus | tostring) end),
      ([.pendingCommands[]?] | map(.command // .) | join(",")),
      (.lastSeenAt // "")
    ])
  ) | @tsv
end
# runner-verdict.jq — S5 convergence verdict for one runner.
# Input:  { "runner": <runner object from GET /runners>, "fixInBuild": <true|false|null> }
#   fixInBuild is computed by the shell with `git merge-base --is-ancestor
#   <fixCommit> <buildSha>` (null when no build sha is reported or the sha is
#   unknown to the local repo) — a version string alone proves nothing.
# Converged = runnerVersion >= 0.2.x AND the running build contains the fix.
def semverAtLeast($v; $min): ($v | split(".") | map(tonumber? // 0)) >= ($min | split(".") | map(tonumber? // 0));

. as $in | $in.runner as $r |
(semverAtLeast($r.runnerVersion // "0"; "0.2.0")) as $versionOk |
{
  runnerId: $r.runnerId,
  status: $r.status,
  runnerVersion: $r.runnerVersion,
  buildSha: ($r.facts.versions.build.sha // null),
  recommendedVersion: $r.recommendedVersion,
  updateAvailable: $r.updateAvailable,
  versionOk: $versionOk,
  fixInBuild: $in.fixInBuild,
  converged: ($versionOk and ($in.fixInBuild == true)),
  reasons: (
    (if $versionOk then [] else ["runnerVersion \($r.runnerVersion // "?") is below 0.2.0"] end)
    + (if $in.fixInBuild == true then []
       elif $in.fixInBuild == false then ["running build \($r.facts.versions.build.sha // "?") does not contain the deterministic-git-failure fix commit"]
       else ["no build sha reported (or unknown locally) — cannot verify the fix is in the running build"] end)
  )
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# server2-ssh.sh <remote command...> — run a command on the server2-alpha host
# (server2@192.168.1.172) using the password file ~/.passwrd WITHOUT ever
# printing, logging, or putting it on a command line (server2-ssh skill rules).
#
# Method: sshpass -f when installed (reads the file directly); otherwise a
# pexpect driver that opens the file inside Python and answers the prompt.
#
# Failure behaviour (this matters: a failed remote probe must not look like a
# success to the caller):
#   - no command given            -> usage on stderr, exit 64
#   - password file missing/empty  -> FATAL on stderr, exit 66 (contents never shown)
#   - password file not mode 600   -> warning on stderr (contents never shown)
#   - connect/auth timeout         -> FATAL on stderr, partial output kept, exit 124
#   - otherwise the REMOTE exit code is propagated (ssh does this natively;
#     the pexpect path reads child.exitstatus/signalstatus)
#
# Read-only usage only in this task (S5 observe-only, survey q9: never
# restart/update/reap anything on the runner hosts from here).
set -euo pipefail

PASSWORD_FILE="$HOME/.passwrd"
SSH_TARGET="server2@192.168.1.172"
SSH_OPTS=(-o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ConnectTimeout=15)

if [ $# -lt 1 ]; then
  echo "usage: server2-ssh.sh '<remote command>'" >&2
  exit 64
fi
if [ ! -f "$PASSWORD_FILE" ]; then
  echo "FATAL: password file $PASSWORD_FILE not found (expected mode 600, first line = password)" >&2
  exit 66
fi
MODE="$(stat -c %a "$PASSWORD_FILE")"
if [ "$MODE" != "600" ]; then
  echo "WARN: $PASSWORD_FILE has mode $MODE, expected 600 — tighten it with: chmod 600 $PASSWORD_FILE" >&2
fi

if command -v sshpass >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  # sshpass consumes the file itself; the password never enters argv or env.
  exec sshpass -f "$PASSWORD_FILE" ssh "${SSH_OPTS[@]}" "$SSH_TARGET" "$@"
fi

python3 - "$@" <<'PY'
import pathlib
import sys

import pexpect

password_file = pathlib.Path.home() / ".passwrd"
try:
    password = [REDACTED]().splitlines()[0].strip()
except OSError as exc:
    print(f"FATAL: cannot read {password_file}: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(66)
if not password:
    print(f"FATAL: {password_file} is empty", file=sys.stderr)
    sys.exit(66)

remote_cmd = " ".join(sys.argv[1:]) or "echo ok"
child = pexpect.spawn(
    "ssh -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new -o ConnectTimeout=15 server2@192.168.1.172 "
    + repr(remote_cmd),
    encoding="utf-8",
    timeout=120,
)
# No logfile is set: nothing pexpect sees (including the prompt exchange) is
# ever written anywhere.
index = child.expect(["[Pp]assword:", pexpect.EOF, pexpect.TIMEOUT])
if index == 0:
    child.sendline(password)
    index = child.expect([pexpect.EOF, pexpect.TIMEOUT])
if index == 2:  # timed out (either before or after the password prompt)
    print(child.before or "", end="")
    print("FATAL: ssh to server2@192.168.1.172 timed out", file=sys.stderr)
    child.close(force=True)
    sys.exit(124)

for line in (child.before or "").splitlines():
    if "Warning: Permanently added" in line:
        continue
    print(line)

child.close(force=True)
if child.exitstatus is not None:
    sys.exit(child.exitstatus)
if child.signalstatus is not None:
    sys.exit(128 + child.signalstatus)
sys.exit(1)
PY

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""mock-api.py — a tiny local stand-in for the KainBain backend API, used ONLY
by bin/tests/run-tests.sh so the ops scripts can be integration-tested without
touching prod.

Routes:
  GET /tasks?projectId=...   -> [{"id": <name>}, ...] for every <name>.json in
                                --tasks-dir ([] when MOCK_EMPTY=1)
  GET /tasks/<id>?projectId=... -> the contents of <id>.json (200);
                                500 when <id> is in MOCK_FAIL_IDS;
                                200 + invalid JSON when <id> == MOCK_BADJSON_ID
  GET /runners               -> contents of --runners-file (200)
  GET /deploy/status         -> contents of --deploy-file (200)

--port 0 picks a free port and writes it to --port-file once listening.
"""
import argparse
import json
import os
import pathlib
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, ThreadingHTTPServer
from urllib.parse import urlparse, parse_qs

## S5 — Roll out 0.2.x runners and run the fleet before/after recount (ops + verification)

**Covers Cause 5 verification and unlocks diagnosis of Causes 3–4.** Deployed runners
are 0.1.0 (main `f430f53`, 11-11); repo is 0.2.0 with interrupt reasons and
deterministic-git-failure handling (`046a6391`, merged 11-21 09:38 in `7ac148ce`).
Rollout is backend-nudged, at most daily per runner, idle-converge
(`docs/runner-update-runbook.md`), so lag is expected — but until it lands, every new
interrupt is still bare and every commit-hook rejection still crash-loops.

**Proposed steps:**
1. Confirm both runners (`local-alpha`, `server2-alpha`) converge to the build
   containing `046a6391` per the runbook; record `GET /runners` versions before/after.
2. Re-run the `WIDE_NET_ANALYSIS.md §2` counts + GUIDE-07 §5 fleet script: bare
   interrupts should drop to ~0, reasons should name Causes 1/3/4 directly, and
   deterministic commit failures should surface as FAILED completions with
   `gitFailure` payloads, never as interrupts.
3. Run the E5 forensics sweep (GUIDE-05 §4): for each remaining post-`finished`
   interrupt, check `kb-<taskId>` worktrees (`158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`,
   `7f6220c3`) for stage-output-commit presence (present → Cause 2/4 territory;
   absent → Cause 5). Only if E5 finds commit-loop cases the `046a6391` fix does not
   cover should a new Cause-5 code task be created.
4. Record the post-rollout counts in the task folder as the new baseline for S1–S4.

**How to confirm the underlying bugs:** this task *is* the confirmation harness —
before/after counts plus the journal sweeps (E3 `Backend 413`, E4 502/fetch-fail,
E5 hook/commit lines). No new unit tests; deliverable is the recount + version record.
**Parallel/blocking:** runs in parallel with all code work; only prod *confirmation*
of S3/S4/S2-runner-half waits on it.
**Risk:** low. Follow the runbook; do not force-restart runners mid-assignment to
speed convergence (observe only — forced restarts are PROD-ACTION and risk new
interrupts, which is exactly what we are measuring).

# Runner update runbook

Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.

## Cutting a runner release (normal path)

The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.

1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).

## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)

When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:

```
git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
```

Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
version forward instead.

## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)

1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
   resolves to the prior tag.
2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
   is cut.

Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
fleet converged.

## Migrating a host to the wrapper

Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
so the fleet version does not change).

Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:

```
# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service

# 2. Rehearse:
scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id> --dry-run

# 3. Migrate (snapshots unit + env, reloads, restarts, re-verifies):
scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id>
```

The script refuses to overwrite an existing `current` link and prints
revert commands (copy the `.bak-<timestamp>` files back, reload,
restart). New installs need no migration: both installers
(`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`) already write
wrapper-based units. Verify after: `doctor` reports `status: ok` with
`entrypoint: wrapper`, and the next heartbeat shows the same version
as before.

## Restart vs Update (Settings › Runners)

Two separate actions, never combined:

- **Restart** reboots the runner on its **current version** — no update
  check runs. It is destructive: any work running on that runner is
  stopped at once (the claim lease expires so the work re-queues, like a
  crash). The confirm window names the runner and warns about running
  work; use it when a runner looks stuck, not to change versions.
  Mechanism: the daemon writes a `restart-requested` sentinel beside the
  install root and exits 0; the wrapper consumes it and boots the SAME
  tree again. Restart therefore needs the wrapper entrypoint — a runner
  started as bare `node main.js` exits without rebooting (migrate to the
  wrapper, above).
- **Update** reinstalls the runner onto its **target version** — the
  exact pin when the runner is pinned, otherwise the newest compatible
  release — and applies only when the runner is idle (never interrupts
  work). A busy runner queues the update for the next idle point.

## Per-runner version setting

Each runner is set to **Latest** (default) or one exact release, via
the version dropdown on its Settings › Runners detail panel:

- **Latest** tracks the newest release. It auto-updates at the next

# Runner update runbook

Operator procedures for the runner self-update channel (Option A,
`docs/adr/0012-runner-artifact-update-channel.md`): cutting releases,
rolling back, migrating hosts to the wrapper, and triaging a runner
that says out of date. The backend directs version selection but never
serves runner bytes (R05) — every procedure below preserves that.

## Cutting a runner release (normal path)

The tag is the version source of truth; the pipeline cuts it.

1. Bump `runnerVersion` in `runner/version.json` (plain semver for
   fleet releases, e.g. `0.2.0`; suffixed tags like `0.3.0-rc.1` for
   canaries — v1 runners skip pre-releases automatically).
2. If the release needs a newer backend API, update the
   `requires.backendApi` range in the same file (e.g.
   `>=1.0.0 <2.0.0`). The release builder refuses manifests without a
   compat claim, and runners filter on this range.
3. Merge to the main line through the normal review flow.
4. Publish the runner (`publish.sh` with the runner component). The
   publish cuts and pushes the annotated `runner-vX.Y.Z` tag, which
   triggers `runner-release.yml`: full update-channel test gate, four
   platform archives, signed `manifest.json` + `.minisig`, GitHub
   release. Re-publishing an unchanged runner is a no-op success (the
   tag already exists, so nothing is re-cut).
5. Raise `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` to the new version on
   the backend. That is the one managed place: trailers light the
   "update available" badge and the backend auto-nudges command-capable
   ones (`requestUpdate`, at most daily per runner). Runners converge
   on idle with no SSH. Leave `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` alone
   unless this is a breaking release (the 409 floor stops dispatch).

## Cutting a runner release (emergency path)

When the pipeline cannot cut the tag (CI down, urgent patch), tag by
hand from the release commit — the same builder runs:

```
git tag -a runner-vX.Y.Z -m "Runner runner-vX.Y.Z" <full-sha>
git push origin runner-vX.Y.Z
```

Then follow step 5 above. Never move an existing tag: cut a patch
version forward instead.

## Rollback drill (bad release, no host access needed)

1. Delete (or un-publish) the bad GitHub release so `releases/latest`
   resolves to the prior tag.
2. Lower `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_RECOMMENDED_VERSION` (and
   `KAINBAIN_RUNNER_MIN_VERSION` if it was raised past the bad
   version) to stop badge nagging and 409 loops.
3. Cut a patch release forward (normal path above). The updater never
   downgrades: runners still on older versions pick the prior release
   up on their next idle check, while runners already on the bad
   release stay there until the patch supersedes it.
4. Two automatic outs: a release that crashes on boot rolls itself
   back to `previous` after 3 failed boots, and raising the min knob
   above the bad version stops it dispatching (409) while the patch
   is cut.

Drill timing to record: un-publish → badges clear, patch cut →
fleet converged.

## Migrating a host to the wrapper

Direct `node main.js` units re-exec the same old directory on every
restart, so staged updates can never boot there. The migration lays a
versioned install root from the running tree and repoints the unit at
the stable wrapper shim — onto the SAME version (no update is staged,
so the fleet version does not change).

Per host, idle runners first; drain busy runners, then migrate:

```
# 1. Pre-check (read-only, safe any time):
KAINBAIN_RUNNER_INSTALL_ROOT=$HOME/.kainbain/runner-install \
  /path/to/runner/bin/kainbain-runner doctor --unit kainbain-runner-<id>.service

# 2. Rehearse:
scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id> --dry-run

# 3. Migrate (snapshots unit + env, reloads, restarts, re-verifies):
scripts/migrate-runner-to-wrapper.sh --id <id>
```

The script refuses to overwrite an existing `current` link and prints
revert commands (copy the `.bak-<timestamp>` files back, reload,
restart). New installs need no migration: both installers
(`scripts/install-local-runner.sh`, `startRunner.sh`) already write
wrapper-based units. Verify after: `doctor` reports `status: ok` with
`entrypoint: wrapper`, and the next heartbeat shows the same version
as before.

## Restart vs Update (Settings › Runners)

Two separate actions, never combined:

- **Restart** reboots the runner on its **current version** — no update
  check runs. It is destructive: any work running on that runner is
  stopped at once (the claim lease expires so the work re-queues, like a
  crash). The confirm window names the runner and warns about running
  work; use it when a runner looks stuck, not to change versions.
  Mechanism: the daemon writes a `restart-requested` sentinel beside the
  install root and exits 0; the wrapper consumes it and boots the SAME
  tree again. Restart therefore needs the wrapper entrypoint — a runner
  started as bare `node main.js` exits without rebooting (migrate to the
  wrapper, above).
- **Update** reinstalls the runner onto its **target version** — the
  exact pin when the runner is pinned, otherwise the newest compatible
  release — and applies only when the runner is idle (never interrupts
  work). A busy runner queues the update for the next idle point.

## Per-runner version setting

Each runner is set to **Latest** (default) or one exact release, via
the version dropdown on its Settings › Runners detail panel:

- **Latest** tracks the newest release. It auto-updates at the next

### Cause 5 — Stage-end commit/push failure crash loop (pre-commit hooks, git faults)

**Summary.** A stage-end `commitAndPush` failure on the 0.1.0 build takes the
generic interrupt+rethrow path: bare interrupt, `exit(1)`, systemd restart,
re-claim, re-run, same failure — the classic crash loop. Deterministic faults
(pre-commit hook rejecting files, e.g. corrupt PNGs) loop forever until the
death bound parks the task. This is the documented "10,000 restarts" incident
class.

**Pros (for).**
- Documented precedent: task `1cae113f` survey (Round 1, Q2) states "the runner
  restarted over 10,000 times in a crash loop after the commit failed", with
  corrupt images vs the pre-commit hook as the trigger (Q6); the fix
  (deterministic-failure → failed completion, no crash; `046a6391`) merged
  11-21 09:38 — after every observed interruption — and still needs runner
  rollout.
- Code path exists and is fatal on the deployed build (generic catch at
  `runner/daemon.js:2441-2452`; the 0.1.0 build predates the
  `isDeterministicGitFailure` branch).
- Comment trail in code already links rethrow-on-git-fault to "crash-loops
  under Restart=always" (`runner/daemon.js:2322-2324`) and restart storms to
  task death loops (`runner/daemon.js:2301-2303`, ref `e79b1d25`).
- `db49d6c6` ("Fix runner recovery commits failing on pre-commit hooks") shows
  hook/commit friction is a live, recurring theme, not a one-off.

**Cons (against).**
--
| E3 | `Backend 413` journal sweep, both hosts, all dates | runner journals | Cause 2 scope beyond `7f6220c3` |
| E4 | Timestamp-join 502/`fetch failed` crashes vs server2-alpha interrupts | this host journal (have) + task histories (have) | Cause 4 per-case proof |
| E5 | Stage-output-commit presence per post-`finished` interrupt | `kb-<taskId>` worktrees (`158394ab`, `db49d6c6`, `1cae113f`, `7f6220c3` preserved) | Cause 5 vs Cause 2/4 split |
| E6 | local-alpha build provenance + post-0.2.x bare-interrupt recount | fleet versions; re-run §2 counts after rollout | whether rollout resolves the bare 69 |
